entries.title: Devil Allies: which printing wins
entries.question: Devil Allies: keep the current book (rank 6 now, heightening from level 14 up to rank 10), or copy Wanderer's Guide's older printing (rank 5, heightening from level 16 to rank 8)?
entries.printed: "You gain summon fiend as a 6th-rank innate spell of a tradition of your choice, which you can cast once per day... At 14th level and every 2 levels thereafter, the spell is heightened by one rank (to a maximum of 10th rank when you reach 20th level)."
entries.aonDoc: C:/wonderers guide/aon-2e-archive/data/by-category/hellknight-order/hellknight-order-9.json (Hellfire Dispatches, Order of the Gate)
entries.wg: Rank 5 until level 16, then 6, 7 and 8 - the older Character Guide numbers.
entries.app: Rank 6, heightening to 7, 8, 9 and 10 at levels 14, 16, 18 and 20.
entries.recommendation: Keep the app. The current book prints rank 6 and heightening from level 14; Wanderer's Guide is on the superseded Character Guide text.
entries.why: Both printings are in the mirror. The Character Guide one is from 2019 and says rank 5, level 16, max rank 8. Hellfire Dispatches reprinted all seven Hellknight orders in 2026 and raised it to rank 6 from level 14. The app matches the 2026 text sentence for sentence. Wanderer's Guide is not inventing - it is simply still on the old book, so a group playing only the Character Guide would see their numbers.
entries.ifYes: Nothing changes; the app already does this.
entries.needsGuy: Only he can say whether the app follows the newest printing or stays glued to Wanderer's Guide when two printings differ.

entries.title: Animist slots at levels 13 to 18
entries.question: Animist prepared spell slots at levels 13 to 18: keep the app's ladder, which matches the printed table, instead of Wanderer's Guide's one-level-later ladder? Yes or no.
entries.printed: Class table: "13 ... 7th-rank spells", "15 ... 8th-rank spells", "17 ... 9th-rank spells"; the Animist Spells per Day table's level-13 row prints "1+1" under 7th.
entries.wg: First 7th, 8th and 9th slot arrive at levels 14, 16 and 18 - one level late.
entries.app: First slot at 13, 15 and 17; second at 14, 16 and 18. Matches the table exactly.
entries.recommendation: Keep the app. The printed table gives the first 7th-rank slot at level 13, 8th at 15, 9th at 17. Wanderer's Guide is a level late.
entries.why: The book's own two tables agree with each other and settle all six disputed levels. I read all twenty rows of the slot table and the app's ladder matches every one of them.
entries.ifYes: Nothing changes; animists keep their high-rank slots a level earlier, exactly as printed.
entries.needsGuy: Only he can approve differing from Wanderer's Guide, even where the printed table leaves no room for argument.

entries.title: Fear No Law: Strike or save upgrade
entries.question: Fear No Law, Fear No One: keep the current book's one-action Strike that calms nearby allies, or switch to the older book's "a success on a fear save becomes a critical success"?
entries.printed: "Make a Strike. If you hit and deal damage, each ally within a 20-foot emanation around you who can see you reduces the value of their frightened condition by 1."
entries.aonDoc: C:/wonderers guide/aon-2e-archive/data/by-category/hellknight-order/hellknight-order-14.json (Hellfire Dispatches, Order of the Scourge)
entries.wg: The older Character Guide version: a fear-save success becomes a critical success. No Strike, nothing for allies.
entries.app: The current one-action Strike that lowers nearby allies' frightened value. No save upgrade.
entries.recommendation: Keep the app's Strike. Correction: Wanderer's Guide is not inventing - it encodes the superseded Character Guide printing of this same order benefit.
entries.why: The earlier note said this text exists nowhere in print; it does. The 2019 Character Guide version reads "When you roll a success on a save against a fear effect, you get a critical success instead", and it also reduced any frightened you gained by 1. Hellfire Dispatches replaced that whole benefit with the Strike in 2026.
entries.ifYes: Nothing changes; Scourge Hellknights keep the Strike and gain no fear-save upgrade.
entries.needsGuy: Only he can rule that a superseded printing Wanderer's Guide still ships is not a reason to change the app.

entries.title: Locate Lawbreakers: who gets rank 5
entries.question: At level 14, does Locate heighten to rank 5 only for Order of the Gate members, as printed, or for every Hellknight holding this benefit, as Wanderer's Guide does?
entries.printed: "If you're a member of the Order of the Gate, when you reach 14th level, the spell is heightened to 5th rank."
entries.aonDoc: C:/wonderers guide/aon-2e-archive/data/by-category/hellknight-order/hellknight-order-9.json (Hellfire Dispatches, Order of the Gate)
entries.wg: Rank 3 below level 14, rank 5 from 14, for everyone. No order check at all.
entries.app: Tradition pick and the once-a-day Locate are built. The heightening is only a note; nothing reads the chosen order.
entries.recommendation: Follow print: heighten to rank 5 at level 14 only for Order of the Gate members. The app already stores which order the player picked.
entries.why: The clause is not idle wording: Order Cross-Training, a level 12 Hellknight feat, lets a Hellknight of any other order take this same lesser order benefit, and it can be taken more than once. That is exactly who the clause excludes. Wanderer's Guide's version hands them the rank-5 spell too.
entries.ifYes: Gate Hellknights get a real rank-5 Locate at 14; cross-trained Hellknights of other orders keep rank 3.
entries.needsGuy: Only he can approve differing from Wanderer's Guide, and confirm the app should start reading the order the player already picked.

entries.title: Steady Balance: Grab an Edge clause
entries.question: Steady Balance: keep only the current book's two clauses, or also add Wanderer's Guide's "Acrobatics instead of a Reflex save to Grab an Edge"?
entries.printed: "Whenever you roll a success using the Balance action, you get a critical success instead. You're not off-guard while attempting to Balance on narrow surfaces and uneven ground."
entries.wg: The printed clause, plus an Acrobatics-for-Reflex substitution on Grab an Edge.
entries.app: Success on Balance becomes a critical success; the off-guard clause is description text only.
entries.recommendation: Keep the app. Correction: that substitution is printed, in the Core Rulebook version of this feat, which Player Core deliberately dropped. Do not add it.
entries.why: The earlier note said the substitution appears nowhere in print; it appears in feat-845, the 2019 Core Rulebook printing of the same feat, whose last sentence is the Grab an Edge clause. Player Core kept the first two sentences and deleted that one.
entries.ifYes: Nothing changes; Steady Balance keeps its two printed effects.
entries.needsGuy: Only he can rule that a clause the Remaster deleted stays deleted even though Wanderer's Guide still ships it.

entries.title: Armor in Earth: armour proficiency
entries.question: The stone armour is medium armour but uses your highest armour proficiency. How should the app work that out, and does the kineticist become trained in medium armour?
entries.printed: "Stone encases you like armor. The stone armor is medium armor but uses your highest armor proficiency." At 3rd level it becomes heavy armour. No sentence anywhere trains the kineticist in medium or heavy armour.
entries.wg: They hand over the same two armour items, and each item trains the wearer in medium armour (the heavy one in heavy armour). That makes the AC come out right, and also lets a kineticist wear real plate and half plate.
entries.app: The two armour items with the right statistics and no proficiency at all, plus a note telling the player to sort it out by hand. A kineticist is untrained in medium and heavy armour, so the AC is wrong today unless the player fixes it themselves.
entries.recommendation: Follow the printed rule, and give Hardwood Armor (desk 26) the same answer in the same breath. The armour should use the wearer's best armour proficiency by itself, on the medium and the heavy version alike, and the kineticist should gain no training in medium or heavy armour. Do not copy Wanderer's Guide's shortcut.
entries.why: "Uses your highest armor proficiency" is not the same as being trained in medium armour, and only that reading leaves ordinary armour untouched. Correction to the earlier note: it said the borrowing idea in the app is locked to inventor armour innovations. It is not — the app has a general best-proficiency borrowing that Sentinel Dedication and Mountain Skin both use. What it does not have is a way to hang that borrowing on an armour the impulse hands over rather than on a whole armour category, and that is the small missing piece. Wanderer's Guide's reading is a defensible shortcut, but it gives the kineticist armour the book never gives them.
entries.ifYes: Attach the existing best-proficiency borrowing to the granted armour item, on Armor in Earth and Hardwood Armor together, and drop the "set it yourself" note from both records.
entries.needsGuy: Yes — it is a small piece of new work and it makes the app differ from Wanderer's Guide, so he should say go before it is built. One word covers both records.

entries.title: Benefactor's Resistance: the dragon bonus, and the floor of 1
entries.question: Should the app copy Wanderer's Guide's extra resistance against dragons, and may the app keep flooring the resistance at 1 when the page prints no minimum?
entries.printed: "You gain resistance equal to half your level to the damage type dealt by the breath of your draconic benefactor… If your draconic benefactor's breath deals bludgeoning, piercing, or slashing damage, instead of gaining resistance to that type, you must choose acid, cold, fire, electricity, or sonic." No minimum is printed, and there is no clause about dragons anywhere.
entries.wg: For every breath type they emit four effects: resistance 1 plus resistance half your level to that type, AND resistance 2 plus resistance equal to your full level to that same type from dragons.
entries.app: One pick over ten damage types, each granting resistance equal to half the character's level with a floor of 1. Nothing about dragons.
entries.recommendation: Keep the app's reading of the damage type and drop their dragon half — no printed text anywhere grants extra resistance against dragons. But record the one place the app goes past the book: the printed sentence is a plain "half your level" with no minimum, so a strict reading gives 0 at 1st level and the app writes 1. That floor is his to allow or remove.
entries.why: Both printed entries were read in full. The feat's only other sentence handles a physical breath weapon, and the Dragonscaled Kobold heritage gives extra Hit Points and a +1 bonus to saves against dragon breath, sleep and paralysed — a save bonus, not resistance. On the floor: the page says only "resistance equal to half your level". Wanderer's Guide reaches 1 by adding two effects together and the app writes the floor straight in, so the two apps agree with each other and neither agrees with the page. That is why it should be recorded rather than quietly kept — every other record on this desk where the app goes past the printed page is on the desk for exactly that reason.
entries.ifYes: Leave the dragon half out and write it down as a known difference from Wanderer's Guide. If he wants the printed reading, remove the floor so a 1st-level kobold has resistance 0; if he wants the floor kept, record it as an allowed exception so it stops coming back.
entries.needsGuy: Yes — for the floor of 1 only. The dragon half needs no ruling.

entries.title: Molten Wit: one question or two
entries.question: Molten Wit: keep tying the skill feat to the skill you pick, or ask for the skill feat as its own separate question the way Wanderer's Guide does?
entries.printed: "You either become trained in Deception and gain the Charming Liar skill feat, or you become trained in Diplomacy and gain the Group Impression skill feat. If you're already trained in one of these skills, you must take the other and can choose from either skill feat. If you're trained in both skills, you become trained in a different skill of your choice instead and can choose from either skill feat."
entries.wg: Two separate questions: pick the skill, then pick either skill feat freely.
entries.app: One question. Deception gives Charming Liar, Diplomacy gives Group Impression, always paired. No branch for a character already trained in either skill.
entries.recommendation: Follow print. Keep the pairing for a character trained in neither skill, and add the two branches the book prints: already trained in one - they must take the other skill and may pick either feat; trained in both - they get a free skill of their choice and may pick either feat.
entries.why: The book pairs skill and feat only in the base case, and both other sentences say plainly "can choose from either skill feat". Wanderer's Guide's two open questions get those two branches right and the base case wrong - their shape lets a player take Diplomacy with Charming Liar, which the book does not allow, and never gives the free skill to someone trained in both.
entries.ifYes: Most players still see one question. A player already trained in Deception or Diplomacy gets a free choice of feat, and one trained in both also gets a free skill.
entries.needsGuy: Only he can decide whether to build the two branches or accept Wanderer's Guide's simpler two-question shape.

entries.title: Firework Technician: throwable vials
entries.question: Should Firework Technician Dedication give the player actual throwable pyrotechnic vials (a fire bomb item), instead of only a counter with nothing attached? Yes or no.
entries.printed: "...creating up to 4 pyrotechnic versatile vials during your daily preparations. These vials have the fire trait and deal fire damage instead of acid... You can use pyrotechnic versatile vials only to throw as bombs, for the Launch Fireworks action (see below), or with Quick Alchemy to create fireworks consumables..."
entries.aonDoc: C:/wonderers guide/aon-2e-archive/data/by-category/feat/feat-8528.json (Guns & Gears Remastered, the current printing; AoN marks feat-3245 as superseded)
entries.wg: Gives a real item, Pyrotechnic Versatile Vials: martial bomb, fire damage, range 20.
entries.app: A counter of 4 vials only. No item exists, so there is nothing to throw. The description already shows the current text; only the record's book link still points at the superseded printing.
entries.recommendation: Follow print and Wanderer's Guide: add a pyrotechnic copy of the existing Versatile Vial item (fire damage instead of acid, thrown, range 20). Also point the record at feat-8528, not the superseded feat-3245.
entries.why: The book says the vials are thrown as bombs, so the player needs a real weapon entry, not just a number. The app already ships a Versatile Vial item to copy from. Nothing is lost by the repoint: the Alchemical Crafting feat the app grants comes from the shared "quick alchemy benefits" rule, which the new printing still uses.
entries.ifYes: The player can throw fire vials straight from the sheet instead of tracking a count with nothing to spend it on.
entries.needsGuy: Only he can approve authoring a new item and moving the record onto the newer printing.

entries.title: Hellknight Dedication: armor training
entries.question: Hellknight Dedication: keep the current book's mental resistance and conditional Intimidation, or add Wanderer's Guide's armor training and always-expert Intimidation? Yes or no.
entries.printed: "You gain resistance to mental damage equal to 1 + your number of archetype class feats from the Hellknight archetype. You become trained in Intimidation; if you were already trained, you become an expert instead."
entries.aonDoc: C:/wonderers guide/aon-2e-archive/data/by-category/feat/feat-8812.json (Hellfire Dispatches); armor clause checked in feat-8814
entries.wg: Expert Intimidation always, light, medium and heavy armor training, an armor-scaled Intimidation bonus, no mental resistance.
entries.app: Mental resistance, Intimidation trained (expert if already trained), Additional Lore for Hell, and the order recorded.
entries.recommendation: Keep the app. Correction: their armor training is printed - but it belongs to Armiger's Protection, a separate Hellknight feat, not to the dedication. The app already builds that feat with the same armor training.
entries.why: Armiger's Protection reads "You become trained in light armor and Hellknight breastplate, a medium armor. If you were already trained in light armor and medium armor, you gain training in Hellknight half plate..." - the same step-by-step shape Wanderer's Guide folded into the dedication. Their always-expert Intimidation is the 2019 Character Guide wording. The 2026 dedication carries neither, and has no armor clause anywhere in it.
entries.ifYes: Nothing changes. Hellknights keep mental resistance, and the armor training stays where the book puts it - on Armiger's Protection, which the app already grants.
entries.needsGuy: Only he can rule that the newest printing replaces the older one Wanderer's Guide still ships.

entries.title: Reverse Engineer: drop the +2
entries.question: Reverse Engineer: remove the +2 Crafting bonus, which the remastered text no longer prints, even though Wanderer's Guide still gives it? Yes or no.
entries.printed: "Furthermore, you can use Crafting instead of Thievery to Disable a Device or Pick a Lock." No +2 appears anywhere in the current entry.
entries.aonDoc: C:/wonderers guide/aon-2e-archive/data/by-category/feat/feat-3053.json (Guns & Gears Remastered, 2025); the +2 lives only in feat-8555, the 2021 printing
entries.wg: Keeps the +2 Crafting bonus and writes the other two clauses in as plain text.
entries.app: The Crafting-for-Thievery substitution on the record, plus a +2 Crafting star in the situational bonus list (situationalBonuses.ts line 559). The description shown to the player is already the new text and has no +2 in it.
entries.recommendation: Follow print: delete the +2 star. Keep the Crafting-for-Thievery substitution and show the Critical Crafting clause as text. The +2 is the older printing.
entries.why: The 2021 printing gave a +2 and needed expert Crafting. The 2025 one dropped the +2, lowered the requirement to trained, and swapped in the Critical Crafting reassembly benefit instead. Keeping both over-delivers. Wanderer's Guide's version is only defensible for a group deliberately playing the old book.
entries.ifYes: The player loses a +2 star the current rules no longer grant; the Crafting-for-Thievery substitution stays.
entries.needsGuy: Only he can approve taking a bonus away from existing players when Wanderer's Guide still shows it.

entries.title: Intuitive Crafting: already-have-both case
entries.question: Intuitive Crafting: keep giving a free skill of the player's choice when they already have both Crafting and Specialty Crafting, which Wanderer's Guide does not - and fix the middle case? Yes or no.
entries.printed: "You are trained in Crafting. If you were already trained in Crafting, you instead gain the Specialty Crafting skill feat...; if you have both, you instead become trained in a skill of your choice."
entries.wg: Already trained gets Specialty Crafting; untrained gets Crafting. A character with both gets nothing.
entries.app: Untrained: Crafting trained, correct. Already trained: Specialty Crafting AND a free skill of choice. Already has both: the free skill only, correct.
entries.recommendation: Mostly keep the app, but fix one case. The book says Specialty Crafting replaces the Crafting training - it does not come with a free skill on top. A character already trained in Crafting who does not yet have Specialty Crafting should get the feat only. The other two cases are already right, including the both-already-held free skill that Wanderer's Guide drops.
entries.why: The earlier note said the app already matched print everywhere; it does not. I read both carriers and the code behind them: the Crafting grant carries a "this grant is redundant, so offer a free skill instead" flag, and that flag fires whenever Crafting is already trained - including the case where the book's replacement is the feat, not a skill. Wanderer's Guide gets that middle case right and the both-held case wrong.
entries.ifYes: A character who already has both keeps their free skill. A character trained in Crafting but without Specialty Crafting stops getting an extra free skill on top of the feat.
entries.needsGuy: Only he can confirm the app may keep a benefit Wanderer's Guide does not give, and approve trimming the extra free skill from the middle case.

entries.title: Merchant's Scale: invented skill bonus
entries.question: Merchant's Scale: leave it with no mechanical effect, as printed, or copy Wanderer's Guide's +1 item bonus to seven Recall Knowledge skills?
entries.printed: Print is silent: the whole entry is "Merchant's Scale Source Player Core pg. 290 Price 2 sp Hands 2 Bulk L" - there is no rules body.
entries.wg: +1 item bonus to seven skills, for Recall Knowledge about the value of items, gems and precious metals.
entries.app: A priced object with no text, no bonus and no description at all.
entries.recommendation: Keep it inert. No printed text anywhere grants that bonus - the whole mirror was searched, and both printings are empty. If it should not look blank, show a plain line saying the book prints no rules for this item; do not author flavour text of our own into a printed record.
entries.why: Twelve other Player Core tools are equally bare - bedroll, chalk, mug, rope and so on - so the empty body is the real entry, not a scraping failure. Wanderer's Guide's bonus is a house addition with no printing behind it. Their reading is not unreasonable as a house rule, but it is not the book.
entries.ifYes: Nothing mechanical changes. The item stops looking broken, without the app putting words in the book's mouth.
entries.needsGuy: Only he can rule that an item stays inert when Wanderer's Guide gives it a bonus.

entries.title: Nagaji cantrip: two pickers, one dead
entries.question: Should the cantrip choice be asked once while building the character, or every day at daily preparations?
entries.printed: "During your daily preparations, choose daze, detect magic, or mage hand. Until your next daily preparations, you can cast the chosen spell as an occult innate cantrip." (mage hand is now Telekinetic Hand)
entries.wg: One picker with the three spells, asked once while building the character. They do not model the daily re-choice at all.
entries.app: The same grant, plus a second picker that changes nothing — one live control and one dead one on the same feat.
entries.recommendation: One control, asked at daily preparations, defaulting to yesterday's answer, and it grants the cantrip. Delete the dead build-time picker. Same answer for the other five kitsune and nagaji spell feats (desks 43 and 44).
entries.why: The printed sentence makes this a daily choice, and his Q23 answer puts daily choices in Daily preparations with the last answer as the default. Correction to the earlier note: it offered Wanderer's Guide's single build-time pick as equally defensible, which would have put this record at odds with desks 43 and 44 — both of which put the same question in daily preparations without hedging. Their build-time pick is them doing less than the book rather than reading it differently, so it does not change the answer here, and all six of these feats should get one shape.
entries.ifYes: Move the choice to Daily preparations with yesterday's answer as the default, delete the second picker, and apply the same shape to the other five kitsune and nagaji spell feats.
entries.needsGuy: No — his Q23 answer already covers it. It is on the desk only so the six feats are changed together.

entries.title: Reinforced Chassis: AC rises with level
entries.question: A: keep the app's +3 AC rising to +4 at 5th and +5 at 10th, as printed. B: Wanderer's Guide's flat +3 at every level.
entries.printed: "grants a +3 item bonus to AC with a Dexterity cap of +1. If you are at least 5th level, the item bonus increases to +4 and at 10th level it increases to +5."
entries.wg: One armour item, flat +3 AC, Dex cap +1, no level scaling anywhere.
entries.app: Same armour with +3, then +4 at 5th level and +5 at 10th; already tested.
entries.recommendation: Keep ours. Follow print: +3, +4 at 5th, +5 at 10th. Same call as your 2026-08-22 ruling that the book wins where their data contradicts it.
entries.why: The printed sentence states both increases plainly, and their flat +3 leaves an automaton two points of AC short from 10th level on.
entries.ifYes: Nothing changes; the app already does this. An automaton keeps the correct AC at 5th and 10th level.
entries.needsGuy: It is a straight difference from Wanderer's Guide's data, and he reserved every such call for himself.

entries.title: Sequestered Spell: when innate becomes expert
entries.question: Does the innate spell attack and DC become expert at 12th level, as the general printed rule says, or at 4th level as Wanderer's Guide has it?
entries.printed: "When you gain an innate spell, you become trained in the spell attack modifier and spell DC statistics. At 12th level, these proficiencies increase to expert."
entries.wg: Same cantrip, split into four tradition-gated pickers; expert on a level-4 condition.
entries.app: One picker narrowed to the surki's recorded tradition; trained, then expert at 12th level.
entries.recommendation: Follow print: trained, expert at 12th, which the app already does. Keep our single narrowed picker; filtering the options in a menu is already your standing call.
entries.why: The general Innate Spells rule names 12th level, and this feat's own text adds no earlier increase.
entries.ifYes: Nothing changes; the app already does this.
entries.needsGuy: Their 4th-level step is a deliberate departure from the printed rule, and only he can wave a Wanderer's Guide difference through.

entries.title: Clawdancer: claw Strikes listed twice
entries.question: Should the two claw Strikes come only from the two stances, so each appears once, removing the duplicate copy the dedication itself grants? Yes or no.
entries.printed: Claw Stance: "The only Strikes you can make are frenzied claw unarmed attacks. These deal 1d6 slashing damage, are in the brawling group…"
entries.wg: Each Strike granted once, by its own stance; nothing on the dedication itself.
entries.app: Both Strikes twice over: once from the dedication, again from each stance. The dedication's pair also shows with no stance turned on.
entries.recommendation: Yes. Drop the dedication's copy and keep the Strikes on Claw Stance and Talon Stance, so each shows once and only while that stance is on.
entries.why: The printed text defines each Strike inside its stance's effect, so a clawdancer standing in neither stance should not have them. Wanderer's Guide does exactly the same, so nothing is in dispute.
entries.ifYes: The Strikes tab stops showing Frenzied Claw and Spinning Talon twice; they appear when the matching stance is turned on.
entries.needsGuy: Nothing here differs from Wanderer's Guide, and the feat already requires claws from another source, so he only needs to green-light the change.

entries.title: Shadowcaster: tradition of Cloak of Shadow
entries.question: A: Cloak of Shadow uses the character's own tradition and attribute, as printed. B: pin it to divine keyed on Wisdom, as Wanderer's Guide does.
entries.printed: "Your domain spells from the shadowcaster archetype are of the same tradition as the spells you used to meet the shadowcaster archetype's prerequisites."
entries.wg: Cloak of Shadow, one Focus Point, and casting pinned to divine keyed on Wisdom.
entries.app: Cloak of Shadow, one Focus Point, cast on the character's own tradition and attribute.
entries.recommendation: A, keep ours. The printed sentence ties the tradition to how the character qualified, so a wizard casts it arcane and a bard occult.
entries.why: The only prerequisite is the ability to cast spells, so the tradition really does change from character to character.
entries.ifYes: Nothing changes; the app already does this. An arcane caster keeps casting Cloak of Shadow with their own spell numbers.
entries.needsGuy: It is a plain difference from Wanderer's Guide's data, which he reserved for himself.

entries.title: Soul Warden: expert spell DC at 12th
entries.question: Should the soul warden's divine spell attack and DC rise to expert at 12th level, as Wanderer's Guide has it and the general printed rule says? Yes or no.
entries.printed: "When you gain an innate spell, you become trained in the spell attack modifier and spell DC statistics. At 12th level, these proficiencies increase to expert."
entries.aonDoc: rules/rules-2232 (Player Core p. 298); the feat itself is feat/feat-3466
entries.wg: Same cantrip, source and trained grant, plus expert spell attack and DC at 12th.
entries.app: Trained divine grant, and the innate spells entry already rises to expert at 12th. I read the code and confirmed it.
entries.recommendation: Yes, and nothing needs changing. The book, Wanderer's Guide and the app all give expert at 12th. This one can simply be closed.
entries.why: The dedication's granted cantrip (printed as disrupt undead, now Vitality Lash) is an innate spell, and the printed Innate Spells rule raises those two numbers at 12th level.
entries.ifYes: Nothing changes; a 12th-level soul warden already rolls attacks and sets DCs at expert.
entries.needsGuy: Nothing is in dispute here. He only needs to say it is closed.

entries.title: Favored Terrain: Speed only when it applies
entries.question: A: keep the star on Speed, since the bonus needs unimpeded journey and being in the terrain. B: add Wanderer's Guide's flat +10 feet, always on.
entries.printed: "If you have the unimpeded journey class feature, you gain a second benefit while in your favored terrain… Plains You gain a +10-foot status bonus to your land Speed."
entries.wg: Speed changed from level 2 with no class-feature check and no in-terrain check.
entries.app: A star on Speed naming both conditions; the Speed number itself is not changed.
entries.recommendation: A, keep ours. You already ruled this exact record on 2026-08-22 (the book wins) and that a conditional value is a star, never a real number.
entries.why: Two of the printed conditions are things the sheet cannot see, so a permanent +10 would tell the player a Speed they do not have.
entries.ifYes: Nothing changes; the app already does this. Speed reads true out of terrain, with a star explaining when the bonus applies.
entries.needsGuy: He named this very record in an earlier ruling, so this only needs his word that it stays closed.

entries.title: Hallowed Necromancer: focus spell tradition
entries.question: A: Hallowed Ground follows the character's own spell slots, as printed. B: pin it to divine with Intelligence, as Wanderer's Guide does.
entries.printed: "Focus spells from the hallowed necromancer archetype have the same tradition as your spell slots."
entries.wg: The granted spell plus casting hard-pinned to the divine tradition with Intelligence as the attribute.
entries.app: Hallowed Ground and a Focus Point; the tradition follows the character's own spell slots.
entries.recommendation: A, keep ours. The printed sentence points straight at the character's own slots, and the prerequisite guarantees they have some.
entries.why: An occult caster taking this archetype should keep casting occult; their fixed divine would change both the tradition and the spell's numbers.
entries.ifYes: Nothing changes; the app already does this. An occult caster's Hallowed Ground stays occult.
entries.needsGuy: It is a plain difference from Wanderer's Guide's data, which he reserved for himself.

entries.title: Hardwood Armor: armour proficiency
entries.question: The hardwood armour is medium armour but uses your highest armour proficiency. Which proficiency should the app use?
entries.printed: "Wood and bark grow over your body like armor. This hardwood armor is medium armor but uses your highest armor proficiency." AC Bonus +3, Dex Cap +2, Check Penalty -2, Speed Penalty -5 feet, Strength +2, Bulk 1, group wood.
entries.wg: The same statistics, plus three level-gated steps on the item itself: trained in medium armour below 13th level, expert from 13th to 18th, master from 19th.
entries.app: The same statistics plus the printed armour group, which they do not carry — but no proficiency of any kind, only a note telling the player to set it themselves. The impulse therefore leaves a kineticist worse off than their own armour.
entries.recommendation: Follow the printed rule, and give Armor in Earth (desk 10) the same answer. The armour uses the wearer's best armour proficiency by itself, and the kineticist gains no training in medium or heavy armour.
entries.why: Correction to the earlier note, which said this route is already built and used by Sentinel Dedication and Mountain Skin. Half right: the app does have a general best-proficiency borrowing and those two records do use it — but it is attached to a whole armour category the feat grants, and here it has to attach to the armour the impulse hands over. That attachment is the piece to add, and it is the same piece Armor in Earth needs. Their ladder is defensible on its own — trained, expert at 13th, master at 19th is exactly a kineticist's own light-armour track — so it only differs for a kineticist who raised armour another way, but it also trains them in medium armour, which the book does not.
entries.ifYes: Attach the existing best-proficiency borrowing to the granted armour item, on Hardwood Armor and Armor in Earth together, and drop the "set it yourself" note from both records.
entries.needsGuy: Yes — same answer and same word as desk 10.

entries.title: Psychic Dedication: no Focus Point
entries.question: A: no focus pool from the dedication, since the printed pool belongs to Psi Development at 6th level. B: grant a Focus Point at 2nd, as Wanderer's Guide does.
entries.printed: Psi Development (6th level): "You gain the ability to amp your psi cantrips. If you don't have one, you gain a focus pool of 1 Focus Point"
entries.aonDoc: feat/feat-8395 (the Dedication, feat/feat-8391, never mentions a pool)
entries.wg: Everything the app has, plus one Focus Point granted by the dedication itself.
entries.app: Occultism, one occult psi cantrip, trained spell attack and DC, a recorded conscious mind. No pool.
entries.recommendation: A, keep ours. The pool is printed on Psi Development at 6th level and our record already carries it there. Everything else matches them.
entries.why: Their side moves a 6th-level benefit onto a 2nd-level feat, which contradicts the printed text of both records.
entries.ifYes: Nothing changes; the app already does this. A psychic archetype character gets their Focus Point at 6th level, not 2nd.
entries.needsGuy: It is a plain difference from Wanderer's Guide's data, which he reserved for himself.

entries.title: Shundar-Quah emblem: daily spell missing
entries.question: Should the emblem's once-per-day Thoughtful Gift reach the Spells page, as the printed Activate line says and four of the seven emblems already do? Or should all seven match Wanderer's Guide and cast nothing?
entries.printed: "Frequency once per day; Effect The tattoo casts its spell… The tattoo of the Spire clan depicts a cracked stone with a metal vein inside. It can cast thoughtful gift."
entries.wg: Only the language and Diplomacy half; nothing at all for the daily casting.
entries.app: Language, Diplomacy, a one-action activation and a daily use, but no spell behind them.
entries.recommendation: One answer for all seven. I would finish the family and add the once-per-day Thoughtful Gift, since lyrune, shadde, shriikirri and skoan already carry theirs. The other whole answer is to take the spell off those four.
entries.why: The printed Activate line grants the casting, but your R10 rule says match Wanderer's Guide even when they do less, and here they do nothing. What is certainly wrong is today's state, where the same item behaves differently by clan.
entries.ifYes: The player can cast Thoughtful Gift once a day from the Spells page instead of only reading about it.
entries.needsGuy: The printed text and his R10 rule point opposite ways, and four emblems already went past Wanderer's Guide. Only he can pick the ending.

entries.title: Sklar-Quah emblem: daily spell missing
entries.question: Should the three emblems with no spell be finished, or should the spell come off the four that have one?
entries.printed: The tattoo grants Shoanti, or a +1 item bonus to Diplomacy when speaking Shoanti if you already know it. "Activate — the actions required are the same as those needed to cast its spell; Frequency once per day; Effect The tattoo casts its spell." The Sun clan tattoo casts Concordant Choir.
entries.wg: They carry the record as an item with one branch: if you already know Shoanti, +1 item bonus to Diplomacy when speaking it; otherwise grant Shoanti. They encode nothing at all for the once-per-day spell — the same on all seven emblems.
entries.app: The language and the Diplomacy bonus, both delivered. The spell is missing, and this emblem carries no activation cost at all.
entries.recommendation: One answer for all seven emblems (desks 28, 29 and 30 together), and it must be the same answer for each. Either finish the family — here that means the once-per-day Concordant Choir, with the player free to spend 1, 2 or 3 actions as the spell itself allows — or take the spell off the four emblems that already carry one. What is certainly wrong is today's split.
entries.why: Checked in the app's own data: four of the seven emblems already carry their once-per-day spell (Lyrune, Shadde, Shriikirri and Skoan) and three carry none (Shundar, Sklar and Tamiir), so the same item behaves differently depending on the clan. The printed Activate line grants the casting on all seven; his R10 rule says match Wanderer's Guide even where they do less, and here they do nothing on any of the seven. Both whole answers are consistent; the current half-and-half is not. This emblem also has no activation cost stored, which is why its button does nothing at all.
entries.ifYes: If he says finish them: add the once-per-day spell to Shundar, Sklar and Tamiir, and give Sklar the spell's own 1-to-3 action cost. If he says match Wanderer's Guide: remove the spell from Lyrune, Shadde, Shriikirri and Skoan so all seven are prose only.
entries.needsGuy: Yes — the printed page and his R10 rule point opposite ways, which is exactly when he should decide. One word covers all seven.

Either finish the family — here the once-per-day Tailwind, so the two-action activation the record already shows does what it says — or take the spell off the four emblems that already carry one. What is certainly wrong is today's split.
entries.why: Checked in the app's own data: four of the seven emblems already carry their once-per-day spell and three carry none, so the same item behaves differently depending on the clan. The printed Activate line grants the casting on all seven; his R10 rule says match Wanderer's Guide even where they do less, and here they do nothing on any of the seven. Both whole answers are consistent; the current half-and-half is not. This record is the clearest case of the harm, because it already shows the player a button and a daily use with nothing behind them.

entries.title: Elemental Existence: granting Adopted Ancestry
entries.question: Should the feat hand the player Adopted Ancestry as a free feat, the way the book says (A), or only hide it from the feat list, the way Wanderer's Guide does (B)?
entries.printed: You gain the Adopted Ancestry feat and gain a 1st level oread ancestry feat as a bonus feat, ignoring the limitations of the lineage trait.
entries.wg: Never grants Adopted Ancestry. It hides that feat from the pickable list, grants a 1st-level oread feat, and opens the oread feats.
entries.app: Grants Adopted Ancestry outright, and the granted feat brings its own "choose an ancestry" question. Also offers the 1st-level oread feat and opens oread feats later.
entries.recommendation: Keep ours. Follow the print: hand out Adopted Ancestry as a free feat. Same call as your 2026-08-22 rule that the book wins.
entries.why: The printed sentence says "You gain the Adopted Ancestry feat", which is a grant; their row hides that feat instead, so their player never gets the other ancestry's feats it opens.
entries.ifYes: Nothing changes; the app already grants the feat, asks which ancestry, and opens the oread feats.
entries.needsGuy: You already ruled that the book wins where their data contradicts the print, so this only needs your word that the same call covers this feat.

entries.title: That's Not Natural: which bonus grows
entries.question: When you are master in Survival, does the +2 apply to the initiative bonus (A, what the app does) or to the Perception DC increase (B, what Wanderer's Guide does)?
entries.printed: You gain a +1 circumstance bonus to all initiative checks... In wilderness regions, you also increase your Perception DC by 1 against these types of creatures for the purposes of resolving their Stealth checks. If you're master in Survival, this circumstance bonus increases to +2.
entries.wg: Both the +1 and the +2 sit on Perception, and their upgrade waits on your Perception rank, not on being master in Survival. They give no initiative bonus at all.
entries.app: +1 to your Perception DC that never grows, and the master-Survival +2 sits on the initiative bonus instead.
entries.recommendation: Keep ours: the +2 goes on the initiative bonus, the only thing the printed text actually calls a circumstance bonus.
entries.why: Their reading is defensible too, since the +2 sentence sits right after the Perception one; but their row cannot be copied either way, because it waits on Perception rank where the book says master in Survival.
entries.ifYes: Nothing changes; initiative still rises to +2 at master in Survival and the Perception mark stays at +1.
entries.needsGuy: The printed sentence can be read honestly either way, so someone has to choose which reading the app ships.

entries.title: Versatile Mutation: energy pick at 8th
entries.question: Should the acid/cold/electricity/fire/sonic choice stay hidden until 8th level (A), or keep being asked at 4th when the feat is taken (B)?
entries.printed: At 8th level, choose one of the following: acid, cold, electricity, fire, or sonic damage; when your ostilli Spits Ambient Magic, it can deal that damage type instead
entries.wg: Asks the five-option question only from 8th level; below that it is not asked at all. Each answer only adds wording.
entries.app: Asks at 4th level with no level check; the record is also marked as takable twice.
entries.recommendation: Hold the energy question back until 8th level. The book and Wanderer's Guide agree here, so this is a plain fix rather than a conflict.
entries.why: Both the printed text and their data put the choice at 8th level, and only the app asks it early; the whole printed entry also has no clause letting you take this feat twice.
entries.ifYes: A 4th-level Ostilli Host stops being asked for an energy type they cannot use for four more levels.
entries.needsGuy: It was filed as a Wanderer's Guide conflict by mistake; you only need to say the fix may go in, and whether "takable twice" stays, since the book prints no repeat clause.

entries.title: Sacred Ki: alignment or sanctification
entries.question: The app already asks holy or unholy, the same as Wanderer's Guide. Keep that (A), or rebuild it around this record's older printing, which names chaos, evil, good and law (B)?
entries.printed: When you select this feat, choose chaos, evil, good, or law. Your choice must match one of your deity's alignment components.
entries.wg: Two options, holy and unholy, each only adding wording; no numbers change.
entries.app: The app already asks holy or unholy, with a note quoting the old alignment sentence. The empty copy of the feat the question looked at is a duplicate the app already hides from every list.
entries.recommendation: Keep what the app already shows. Nothing to build and nothing to delete: the picker matches theirs, and the empty twin is already hidden.
entries.why: No deity in this app carries the old alignment components - every deity carries holy or unholy - so the four printed alignments have nothing to match against, while the feat's own sentence still asks the player to choose something.
entries.ifYes: Nothing changes; the monk keeps the holy/unholy question and its note.
entries.needsGuy: Only you can say whether this feat keeps being asked in the newer holy/unholy words while its printed text still names the four old alignments.

entries.title: Ardent Armiger: which printing wins
entries.question: Keep the app's bonus, which follows the newer printing our record holds (A), or switch to Wanderer's Guide's older attitude-and-Coerce version (B)?
entries.printed: You gain a +1 circumstance bonus to saves against effects that could inflict the controlled or frightened conditions.
entries.wg: +1 to all three saves against mental effects that improve your attitude, and to your Will DC against Coerce, Demoralize, Make an Impression or Make a Request.
entries.app: +1 circumstance to all saves against effects that could inflict controlled or frightened.
entries.recommendation: Keep ours. It matches the printed reprint word for word, and their row is the earlier text. The book wins.
entries.why: Our record is the Hellfire Dispatches printing and our bonus is exactly that sentence, so their row is simply stale.
entries.ifYes: Nothing changes. The free-action extra Will save is still only described, not offered as a control.
entries.needsGuy: Your rule is no difference from Wanderer's Guide without your word, even where the book plainly backs us.

entries.title: Devil's Eye: Legal Lore rank
entries.question: Keep expert Legal Lore rising to master and legendary, plus the Objection reaction and the +1 (A), or drop to Wanderer's Guide's trained-only version (B)?
entries.printed: You gain the Objection reaction. You also become an expert in Legal Lore and gain a +1 circumstance bonus to any check you make to read or negotiate a treatise, contract, or similar text. At 7th level you become a master of Legal Lore, and at 15th level you become legendary in Legal Lore.

entries.recommendation: Keep ours. Follow the print exactly. Their row is a full rank short and drops two things the book names.
entries.why: The printed text names expert, the 7th and 15th steps, the reaction and the bonus, and we carry all four.
entries.ifYes: Nothing changes; the app already matches the book on every piece the sentence names.
entries.needsGuy: Your 2026-08-22 rule already says the book wins when their data contradicts the print; this only needs your word that it covers this feat.

entries.title: Gunslinger Mastery: advanced gun rank
entries.question: Keep advanced firearms and crossbows at expert plus critical specialization (A), or follow Wanderer's Guide, putting every firearm and crossbow at master with no critical specialization (B)?
entries.printed: Your proficiency rank increases to master with simple and martial firearms and crossbows. Your proficiency rank for advanced firearms and crossbows, simple weapons, martial weapons, and unarmed attacks increases to expert. You gain access to the critical specialization effects for firearms and crossbows.
entries.wg: The whole firearm and crossbow groups at master, advanced ones included, and no critical specialization at all.
entries.app: Master for simple and martial firearms and crossbows, expert for advanced ones, expert for simple, martial and unarmed weapons, plus critical specialization on firearms and crossbows.

entries.ifYes: Nothing changes; the app already matches the book on all four ranks and on critical specialization.
entries.needsGuy: Keeping ours is a deliberate difference from Wanderer's Guide, which needs your word.

entries.title: Hardened Chassis: missing Enhancement tier
entries.question: Should the printed Enhancement be built and switched on only by an augmentation feat that names this feat (A), or asked of every automaton the way Wanderer's Guide asks it (B)?
entries.printed: Enhancement Your chassis gets even tougher. Choose one of the following benefits: you gain resistance 3 to all physical damage, or your chosen resistance increases to a value equal to half your level (minimum 3). And the automaton rules: "You don't gain the benefits of the enhancement unless you take a feat that grants you those benefits, such as Lesser Augmentation."
entries.aonDoc: C:/wonderers guide/aon-2e-archive/data/by-category/feat/feat-9400.json (the Enhancement rule itself is on the automaton page, ancestry/ancestry-98.json)
entries.wg: Asks "Enhancement?" right on the feat, with a No option, so any automaton can answer yes - and their "increase" answer just adds another 3 instead of half your level.
entries.app: Only the damage-type question with resistance 3. Hardened Chassis is offered inside Lesser and Greater Augmentation, but picking it there only shows a note telling you to work the benefit out yourself.
entries.recommendation: Build the Enhancement so the app computes it, switched on only by an augmentation feat that names this feat. Never ask every automaton.
entries.why: The automaton rules say you do not get an enhancement unless a feat grants it, so their "anyone may say yes" question breaks the printed rule; and this is the same call as your ruling that a question whose answer does nothing is usually a missing piece to build.
entries.ifYes: An automaton who points Lesser or Greater Augmentation at this feat finally gets the better resistance instead of a note.
entries.needsGuy: Their row lets any automaton have the tier, which the printed rule forbids, so this closes under your 2026-08-22 book-wins rule once you say the missing benefit may be built.

entries.title: Weapon Expertise: martial for which classes
entries.question: Keep the per-class split, where only the martial classes gain martial weapons (A), or give every class simple, martial and unarmed (B)?
entries.printed: Your proficiency rank for simple weapons and unarmed attacks increases to expert.
entries.wg: They hold nineteen separate Weapon Expertise records, one per class or group of classes: casters get simple and unarmed at 11th, martial classes get simple, martial and unarmed at 5th. That is our split exactly.
entries.app: Simple, martial and unarmed at 5th for champion, exemplar, guardian, investigator, magus, runesmith, swashbuckler and thaumaturge; simple and unarmed at 11th for druid, witch, wizard, necromancer, kineticist, oracle, psychic and sorcerer.
entries.recommendation: Keep ours, and close this with no ruling. The book prints a separate Weapon Expertise per class, and Wanderer's Guide splits the classes the same way we do.
entries.why: I read all twenty-four printed Weapon Expertise entries (sixteen classes, several printed twice) and their nineteen records: druid, wizard, witch, sorcerer, oracle, psychic, kineticist and necromancer get simple weapons and unarmed attacks only, at 11th.
entries.ifYes: Nothing changes; a wizard or druid still does not get expert martial weapons.
entries.needsGuy: Nothing. The earlier note that they give every class martial weapons came from matching our one shared record against one of their nineteen.

entries.title: Brutality: crit spec melee only
entries.question: Keep critical specialization while raging on melee weapons and unarmed only (A), or extend it to bows and crossbows the way Wanderer's Guide does (B)?
entries.printed: While raging, you have the critical specialization benefits for melee weapons and unarmed attacks.
entries.wg: Simple, martial and unarmed weapon categories while raging, with no melee restriction.
entries.app: Critical specialization while a rage mode is on, melee weapons and unarmed attacks only.
entries.recommendation: Keep ours. The printed sentence says melee weapons and unarmed attacks, so a raging barbarian's longbow should not get it.
entries.why: The word "melee" is in the printed sentence and their encoding simply drops it.
entries.ifYes: Nothing changes; ranged strikes still show no critical specialization from Brutality.
entries.needsGuy: Keeping ours means staying different from Wanderer's Guide, which only you can authorise.

entries.title: Kitsune Spell Mysteries: all three spells
entries.question: Should all three spells be granted as 1st-rank divine innate spells once a day (A), or only Bane, which is all Wanderer's Guide actually sets up (B)?

entries.wg: Only Bane is set up as a divine innate spell; the other two grant nothing usable.

entries.recommendation: Keep all three, divine, 1st rank, once a day, and ask it once - at daily preparations, where the book puts it and where you already ruled daily choices belong.
entries.why: The printed sentence covers all three options equally and their two empty options look like an authoring slip; the same doubled question sits on all six kitsune and nagaji spell feats.
entries.ifYes: The player picks once, at daily preparations, and can change the spell each day.
entries.needsGuy: You decide whether we may keep doing more than Wanderer's Guide here, and whether the six doubled questions are tidied now or later.

entries.title: Nagaji Spell Mysteries: one asking
entries.question: Keep all three spells as 1st-rank occult innate once a day and drop the second question that grants nothing (A), or match Wanderer's Guide's bare version (B)?
entries.printed: During your daily preparations, choose charm , fleet step , or heal . You can cast the chosen spell as a 1st-level occult innate spell once that day.

entries.why: The book names the rank, the tradition, the once-a-day and the daily-preparations timing that their row leaves out entirely.
entries.ifYes: The player is asked once instead of twice and can change the spell each day.

entries.title: Shoony Lore: plain Lore or Additional Lore
entries.question: Keep trained in Shoony Lore only (A), or copy Wanderer's Guide and hand out the whole Additional Lore feat, which adds three extra skill increases (B)?
entries.printed: You also become trained in Shoony Lore.
entries.wg: Diplomacy and Survival trained, plus the whole Additional Lore feat with its extra skill increases at 3rd, 7th and 15th level.

entries.why: Additional Lore is a different feat with extra benefits, and using it as a generic "gain a Lore" tool over-grants and lets the Lore be any subject rather than Shoony.
entries.ifYes: Nothing changes; a shoony still gets three trainings and no bonus skill increases.
entries.needsGuy: Only you can allow us to keep differing from Wanderer's Guide's generic way of granting a Lore skill.

entries.title: Advanced Red Mantis Magic: an old-book feat on a new-book archetype
entries.question: Should this feat give its 2nd, 3rd and 4th-rank spell slots on top of the spellcasting the current Red Mantis feats already give?
entries.printed: "Add two 2nd-level spells to your Red Mantis assassin spellbook. You gain a 2nd-level spell slot… At 8th level… a 3rd-level spell slot. At 10th level… a 4th-level spell slot." This is the 2019 World Guide printing, and it refers to a Red Mantis assassin spellbook.
entries.wg: They carry the legacy printing and grant its slots exactly as written, but hang them on a spellcasting source their own data never defines.
entries.app: Nothing. The app's Red Mantis spell slots all come from the dedication running the ordinary ladder, and this feat grants no slots.
entries.recommendation: Do not add the slots. This is the 2019 World Guide feat and it belongs to a Red Mantis archetype the 2024 book replaced whole. Either drop it from the archetype or leave it as an old-book record that grants nothing, the same way the app already handles other superseded printings.
entries.why: Correction to the earlier note, which said to follow print and add the 4th-rank slot at 10th. Checked in our own data: red-mantis-assassin-dedication, Basic, Expert and Master Red Mantis Magic and Red Mantis School Spell all cite the 2024 Prey for Death printing, and only this one feat still points at the 2019 World Guide page. Checked in the mirror: Prey for Death prints no Advanced Red Mantis Magic at all — it replaced the whole archetype with basic, expert and master spellcasting. So adding the old slot on top of the new ladder puts a player ahead of both books, which the earlier note admitted and then recommended anyway. The 2019 feat also fills a Red Mantis spellbook the 2024 archetype does not have, so its slot has nothing to sit in. This is the same answer as Devil Allies, Fear No Law, Steady Balance and Reverse Engineer: one printing per record, and the superseded book's extras are not added.
entries.ifYes: Mark the feat as belonging to the old book so it grants nothing inside the current Red Mantis archetype, and write the difference from Wanderer's Guide down so it stops coming back.
entries.needsGuy: Yes — it may already be on a character's sheet, so removing what it offers is his call.

entries.title: Agate Ellipsoid: where the resonant note is shown
entries.question: Wanderer's Guide never grants augury twice. Should the app print the resonant sentence on the augury entry, the way they do? Yes or no.
entries.printed: The resonant power causes the augury spell from the aeon stone to always succeed at the DC 6 flat check to give an answer other than "nothing."
entries.wg: One yes/no question, "Is this granting the resonant power?". Both answers grant augury once; the yes answer also prints this sentence on the spell.
entries.app: Grants augury once. The sentence sits in the item's description, and a "Slotted in a wayfinder" mark on the item is what turns the power on.
entries.recommendation: Yes. Keep our wayfinder mark, and print the sentence on the augury entry too. Neither side grants a second spell, so there is no disagreement here.
entries.why: The earlier note that they re-grant augury was a misreading of their data: they grant it once inside each answer. His principle C already puts the note on the spell it changes.
entries.ifYes: A player who marks the stone as slotted reads "always succeeds" on the augury entry itself, not only buried in the item text.
entries.needsGuy: Almost nothing. The clash described in the old note does not exist, so this is a small display fix rather than a ruling.

entries.title: Dusty Rose Prism: note placement and a duplicate control
entries.question: Same as the Agate Ellipsoid, plus one extra: should the older yes/no picker on this one stone go, leaving only the wayfinder mark? Yes or no.
entries.printed: The resonant power increases the damage prevented by your aeon stone's shield spell from 5 to 10.
entries.wg: One yes/no question. Both answers grant shield once; the yes answer also prints this sentence on the shield spell.
entries.app: Grants shield at will, the sentence sits in the item text, and this one stone carries BOTH a wayfinder mark and an older yes/no picker asking the same thing.
entries.recommendation: Yes. Print the 10-damage sentence on the shield entry, and drop the duplicate picker so only the wayfinder mark asks the question.
entries.why: They never grant shield twice, so the old note's choice was a false one. Two controls asking one question on the same item just confuses the player.
entries.ifYes: The player sees the raised block value on the spell itself, and is asked once instead of twice whether the stone is slotted.
entries.needsGuy: Only the duplicate picker is worth a word from him, since three stones carry it and thirty do not.

entries.title: Western Star: where the resonant note is shown
entries.question: Same as the other two stones. Should the app print the resonant sentence on the illusory disguise entry, the way Wanderer's Guide does? Yes or no.
entries.printed: The resonant power allows you to render all of your aeon stones and your wayfinder invisible whenever you use the activation to gain the effects of illusory disguise.
entries.wg: One yes/no question. Both answers grant illusory disguise once; the yes answer also prints this sentence on the spell.
entries.app: Grants the illusory disguise activation. The sentence sits in the item's description, behind the same "Slotted in a wayfinder" mark.
entries.recommendation: Yes. Keep our wayfinder mark, and print the sentence on the illusory disguise entry as well. No second spell exists on either side.
entries.why: Same misreading as the other two stones: their yes answer re-states the item's one spell, it does not add another. The rider belongs where the player reads the spell.
entries.ifYes: The invisibility rider reads on the spell the player actually uses, instead of only in the item's description.
entries.needsGuy: Almost nothing. There is no difference with Wanderer's Guide to authorise, only a small fix to make.

entries.title: Arcana of Iron: expert weapons and a wrong grant
entries.question: Follow print, so martial and advanced weapons reach expert only when the character's class gives weapon expertise, and drop the class feature the app wrongly hands over? Yes or no.
entries.printed: You become trained in advanced weapons. If you gain the weapon expertise class feature, your proficiency in martial and advanced weapons increases to expert.
entries.wg: Expert at character level 13 whatever the class, martial weapons never touched, and the Bespell Strikes 1d8 line carried as text.
entries.app: Trained in advanced weapons forever, no expert step, no Bespell Strikes line, and it wrongly hands over the Weapon Expertise class feature.
entries.recommendation: Follow print. Raise martial and advanced to expert when the class grants weapon expertise, drop the wrong grant, and add the Bespell Strikes 1d8 line they carry and we do not.
entries.why: Our classes grant weapon expertise at 5th or 11th level, never 13th, so their flat 13 is wrong for every one of them. The app already asks this same question for skills.
entries.ifYes: A war mage stops falsely owning Weapon Expertise, reaches expert martial and advanced weapons when their class earns it, and finally reads the 1d8 line.
entries.needsGuy: Only he can approve stepping away from Wanderer's Guide's flat level 13 on the expert step.

entries.title: Astrolabe of Falling Stars: missing +1 star
entries.question: Give this astrolabe the same star its six sibling astrolabes carry, or Wanderer's Guide's version that narrows the +1 to Survival only? A or B.
entries.printed: An astrolabe also grants a +1 item bonus to checks to identify celestial bodies.
entries.wg: A +1 item bonus pinned to Survival, with the celestial-bodies restriction carried as text on the bonus.
entries.app: Nothing on this record. Six sibling astrolabe records carry the star, all of them on every skill.
entries.recommendation: Add the sibling star: +1 item on checks to identify celestial bodies, on all skills. Do not narrow it to Survival.
entries.why: Print names no skill, and our six other astrolabes already star every skill. Their Survival-only reading is defensible too, since only someone trained in Survival can use the thing at all.
entries.ifYes: This astrolabe finally shows its +1 star, and stops being the odd one out among the seven astrolabes.
entries.needsGuy: A reviewer refused the fix because choosing all skills over Wanderer's Guide's Survival takes a side in a rules disagreement.

entries.title: Instinct Ability: their +3 Hit Points
entries.question: Keep the app's grant of the instinct ability, and leave out the +3 Hit Points Wanderer's Guide adds here? Yes or no.
entries.printed: You gain the instinct ability for the instinct you chose for Barbarian Dedication.

entries.app: Grants whichever instinct ability matches the instinct chosen on Barbarian Dedication. No Hit Points.
entries.recommendation: Keep ours, and do not copy their +3. It is one slice of how they pay out Barbarian Resiliency, which he already ruled on (R11) and which our own record already handles.
entries.why: That same +3 sits on nine barbarian archetype feats, which is their way of paying 3 Hit Points per archetype feat. Our Barbarian Resiliency already counts this feat, so copying it would pay twice.
