entries.title: Breath of the Dragon: one exemplar answer
entries.question: Replace the three separate breath pickers with the dragon already chosen on Dragonblood, and which source do we build the table from: the printed pages, Foundry, or dragon stat blocks?
entries.printed: The shape of the breath, the damage type, and the saving throw match those of your draconic exemplar (see above).
entries.wg: Forty rules keyed to the dragon's name, each writing one sentence that states shape, damage and save together. Text only, no numbers.
entries.app: Three separate pickers for shape, damage and save, so illegal breaths are buildable, and the dragon answer the player already gave is ignored.
entries.recommendation: Derive all three from the Dragonblood dragon. Take the eight rows our own pages print, fill the other thirty-two from Foundry, and do not use dragon stat blocks.
entries.why: Print says one answer decides all three. Their crystal row says Will where the printed crystal dragon says Reflex, and stat blocks are no better: the printed sea dragon breathes a 25-foot burst.
entries.ifYes: A player picks their dragon once and the breath fills itself in. Impossible breaths stop being buildable, but saved picks need moving over.
entries.needsGuy: Only he can pick the table's source, accept the differences from Wanderer's Guide on crystal, sea and wish, and accept that saved breath answers are lost.

entries.title: Basic Summoner Spellcasting: which book the archetype is on
entries.question: Should the app be rebuilt to the old bounded rule of two slots, or moved to the 2026 reprint where the archetype casts normally?
entries.printed: The 2021 printing is Feat 6 and grants "the basic bounded spellcasting benefits" — a 1st and a 2nd-rank slot, with the 1st replaced by a 3rd at 10th level. The 2026 Impossible Magic printing is Feat 4 and grants "the basic spellcasting benefits", with no bounded rule at all. The magus twin changed the same way.
entries.wg: Their record sits at level 4, matching the 2026 printing, and runs the ordinary ladder — three levelled slots from 8th onward, all retained, no replacement.
entries.app: The app currently matches them: three retained slots, no replacement.
entries.recommendation: Do not rebuild the app to the old bounded rule. Answer this together with desks 104, 120 and 121 as one decision about which book the magus and summoner are on. Our copy of Archives of Nethys holds the 2026 Impossible Magic printing in full, and on that book Wanderer's Guide is right and the app is already close to it.
entries.why: Correction to the earlier note, which treated the bounded rule as the printed text. It is the 2021 Secrets of Magic text. Both printings are in the mirror and were read side by side: the 2021 feat says "basic bounded spellcasting benefits" at Feat 6, the 2026 one says "basic spellcasting benefits" at Feat 4, and their level even matches Wanderer's Guide's. Rebuilding the app to the bounded rule would move this archetype onto the older book at the same moment desk 121 moves the magus onto the newer one, which is two books in one app.
entries.ifYes: Move the summoner and magus archetypes to the 2026 printing along with the two classes: ordinary spellcasting, basic feat at level 4, and the bounded rule gone. If he prefers to stay on the 2021 book, then desks 104, 120 and 121 must stay there too.
entries.needsGuy: Yes — it is one quarter of a single decision about which book these two classes are on.

entries.title: Time Mage: tradition derived or picked
entries.question: Keep deriving the tradition from the class as print says and fix the innate cantrip, or add Wanderer's Guide's four-way tradition picker? A or B.
entries.printed: This innate spell and your focus spells from the time mage archetype are of the same tradition as the spells you used to meet the archetype's prerequisites.
entries.wg: A free four-way tradition picker, Wisdom as the key attribute on all four answers, and focus and innate spells swapped.
entries.app: Matches print, but the innate Time Sense carries no tradition and falls back to arcane.
entries.recommendation: Keep print, and derive the innate cantrip's tradition the same way the focus side already does. No picker; three of their four answers are illegal.
entries.why: The printed sentence ties the tradition to your class, so a picker would offer three traditions the character cannot legally have. The app already derives a tradition this way for another feat.
entries.ifYes: A divine or primal time mage casts Time Sense on their own tradition instead of arcane, and no new control appears.
entries.needsGuy: His standing rule turns every Wanderer's Guide picker into a visible control here, and that rule collides with the printed text on this record.

entries.title: Pistol Wand: runes on the stock
entries.question: Keep the +1 on Strikes with the pistol wand's stock as printed, or strip it out to mirror Wanderer's Guide exactly? Yes or no.
entries.printed: This +1 flintlock pistol has a reinforced stock permanently attached to it, and the pistol's potency rune (and any other runes) applies to Strikes with the stock as well.
entries.wg: Hands over a plain Reinforced Stock weapon with no rune, so stock Strikes get no bonus.
entries.app: The stock carries a built-in +1 potency, so stock Strikes get the printed bonus.
entries.recommendation: Keep ours. Print says the runes carry over to the stock, and Wanderer's Guide simply hands over the base weapon and loses it.
entries.why: The printed sentence is explicit and their version drops the rune it names. Ours carries the +1, though not the later runes a player etches, which print also passes to the stock.
entries.ifYes: Nothing changes today, though runes etched later on the pistol still will not reach the stock.
entries.needsGuy: Only he can confirm keeping a known difference from Wanderer's Guide rather than mirroring them.

entries.title: Tumbling Theft: Thievery or Stealth
entries.question: Keep the +1 star on Thievery as printed, or move it to Stealth to mirror Wanderer's Guide? A or B.
entries.printed: You gain a +1 circumstance bonus to your Thievery check to Steal as your tumbling make it difficult for your enemy to keep track of your movement.
entries.wg: The +1 lands on Stealth, even though the paragraph they quote says Thievery and their own bonus wording says the Steal.
entries.app: A +1 circumstance star on Thievery for the Steal after a critical Tumble Through.
entries.recommendation: Keep ours. Print and their own quoted paragraph both say Thievery; only the name of the stat they aimed at says Stealth.
entries.why: Three of the four pieces of evidence, including their own quoted text, point at Thievery. Their Stealth target is the odd one out.
entries.ifYes: Nothing changes, the app already does this.
entries.needsGuy: Only he can call an obvious Wanderer's Guide typing mistake a mistake rather than something to copy.

entries.title: Mask of the Mantis (Major): darkvision rank
entries.question: Does the Major mask keep the Greater's 5th-rank spells, or fall back to the base 2nd rank because its own block says nothing? A or B.
entries.printed: The Greater block reads "When you Enhance Vision, the darkvision spell or see the unseen spell is heightened to 5th-rank." The Major block below it adds only the +3 bonus and a Locate Target activation, and says nothing about the rank.
entries.wg: Not consulted. This is a hole in the printed text, not a difference with them.
entries.app: The Major stores both spells at rank 2. The Greater correctly stores rank 5.
entries.recommendation: Raise the Major to 5th rank for both spells. Every other number on the Major goes up, and an 18th-level mask should not cast weaker than the 11th-level one.
entries.why: No earlier ruling covers this, so it is a fresh reading. The book restates a number in the Major block only when it changes, which suggests the rank simply carries over.
entries.ifYes: The Major mask's Enhance Vision sees through magical darkness, just as the cheaper Greater mask already does.
entries.needsGuy: The book never says whether a Major variant keeps the Greater's improvements, so only he can set that reading for every graded item.

entries.title: Zealot Staff: free blast limit
entries.question: Does the Zealot Staff's free-action blast have a use limit? A: no limit, follow the printed page. B: once per 10 minutes, follow the line Foundry adds.
entries.printed: The page has no Frequency line at all: "Activate Free Action (concentrate) Trigger You hit with a Strike using the staff; Effect A vicious blast of deific power explodes as you hit."
entries.wg: Not Wanderer's Guide but Foundry: it adds once per 10 minutes plus two traits. Players never see that text in our app.
entries.app: Ships a once-per-minute limit and a "per minute" pip next to the charge pool - a cadence no source prints.
entries.recommendation: A: follow print. Drop the once-per-minute limit and its pip, and keep only the staff's charge pool.
entries.why: Our once-per-minute matches neither the printed page nor Foundry, and the book wins by his standing rule. He has already refused to build a number out of Foundry alone, on the deviant statistics. Foundry's side would only be defensible if Paizo issued a correction we do not hold.
entries.ifYes: The extra 1d4 spirit damage per damage die fires on every triggering hit, and only the charge pool is counted.
entries.needsGuy: Only he can say whether a line Foundry added counts as a source when the printed page carries no limit at all.

entries.title: Wild Lights: the spell it changes is gone
entries.question: The feat changes Dancing Lights, which the remaster removed. Should the app point it at Light instead?
entries.printed: When you cast Dancing Lights, change its duration to 1 minute and its effect to a single floating light shaped like a Tiny creature, instead of up to four floating lights.
entries.wg: They carry no record for this feat at all.
entries.app: No working piece. The printed sentence was quietly rewritten at import to say "When you cast Light", which is wrong against our Light, and the display still shows "dancing lights", so the rewrite is invisible.
entries.recommendation: Keep it as text, under one rule shared with Toppling Tentacles (desk 71): never rewrite a printed spell name, and attach the feat's mechanical rider to the replacement spell only where the feat's effect still makes sense against it. Here it does not — so put the printed name Dancing Lights back, drop the link to Light, and add one short line clearly marked as ours saying Light is what replaced that spell.
entries.why: The archive itself records Light as the replacement, which is why the retarget happened, and that is the defensible other side. But the feat cuts the duration to 1 minute and reduces four lights to one, and our Light lasts until your next daily preparations and makes one orb — so laid on Light the feat would take something away and change nothing else. Toppling Tentacles is the same shape with the opposite answer, because there the feat's effect still works against the replacement. Quietly rewriting printed text is the part that has to stop either way.
entries.ifYes: Restore the printed spell name, remove the link to Light, and add one clearly-marked line of ours naming the replacement. Apply the same rule to Toppling Tentacles and Spew Tentacles.
entries.needsGuy: Yes — one word from him on how the app handles a feat whose spell was replaced covers this record, Toppling Tentacles and Spew Tentacles together.

entries.title: Toppling Tentacles: which spell carries the note
entries.question: The feat changes Black Tentacles, which is hidden in the app and was replaced by Slither. Where should its note go?
entries.printed: When you cast Black Tentacles, replace the standard effects: spell attack rolls against each creature's Reflex DC; on a success the creature falls prone and takes 3d6 bludgeoning; the tentacles deal 1d6 to creatures already prone; the area is difficult terrain.
entries.wg: They match print exactly — bludgeoning damage, on Black Tentacles.
entries.app: No note anywhere. Black Tentacles is hidden as a superseded spell, and the archive records Slither as its replacement.
entries.recommendation: Both, under the same rule as Wild Lights (desk 70): keep the printed spell name, and attach the rider to the replacement only where the effect still works. So print the note on Black Tentacles as printed, and the same note — named as coming from this feat — on Slither, where it does still work. Fix Spew Tentacles the same way.
entries.why: Print names Black Tentacles and the archive itself records Slither as what replaced it. Black Tentacles is hidden in the app, so a note only there would be read by nobody, and he has ruled that something granted must actually reach the sheet. Unlike Wild Lights, the feat's effect still makes sense against the replacement — both are an area that grabs and damages, so the rider changes it rather than breaking it. Black Tentacles alone is the stricter reading of print, and Wanderer's Guide reads it that way.
entries.ifYes: Put the printed note on Black Tentacles, and the same note marked as coming from this feat on Slither. Do the same for Spew Tentacles.
entries.needsGuy: Yes — the same one word that covers Wild Lights covers this.

entries.title: Screech Shooter greater: wrong DC shown
entries.question: For an upgraded item, do we write one combined sentence ourselves (A), or show the printed base text and then the printed upgrade line word for word (B)?
entries.printed: "A greater screech shooter is a +2 greater striking harmona gun. The DC for the activation is 30 and it affects creatures in a 40-foot emanation." The base page prints "All creatures in a 30-foot emanation from you must attempt a DC 25 Will save."
entries.wg: Not Wanderer's Guide: the archive page inside our own app already carries both the base blurb and the upgrade line, word for word.
entries.app: Greater and major both show the base 30-foot, DC 25 sentence. The first sentence was already rewritten per grade ("+2 greater striking"), so only the numbers were left behind.
entries.recommendation: A: give each grade its own sentence, using only the numbers the book prints for that grade.
entries.why: The app already rewrites that first sentence per grade, so A is the smaller change, and his rule is to pick the wording that leaves the player least confused - B would print DC 25 and DC 30 in the same popup. B is genuinely defensible: it is the book word for word, and the player can already read that on the archive page.
entries.ifYes: Greater and major screech shooters, and the two upgraded wyrm spindles, finally show the right DC and area.
entries.needsGuy: Only he can choose between one tidy sentence we write and the book's two sentences the player has to combine.

entries.title: Armiger's Protection: the free armor pick
entries.question: Delete the broken Hellknight picker and always hand out the breastplate (A), or make it a real pick of the Hellknight armors you are trained in (B)?

entries.recommendation: B: a real pick of Hellknight breastplate, Hellknight half plate and Hellknight plate, with the ones the character is not trained in greyed out and saying why.
entries.why: Print gives a free suit of a type you become trained in, and a character already trained in light and medium armor becomes trained in all three - so A would quietly take two of their options away. He has already ruled that a picker granting nothing is a missing piece, and that an option you cannot take must look unpickable.
entries.ifYes: A Hellknight character picks their free suit and it actually lands in their inventory.
entries.needsGuy: Print settles this one, so a one-word yes is enough - he asked not to spend a ruling on a question with only one correct answer.

entries.recommendation: Keep ours. Do not import their operation.
entries.why: Print lists Labor Lore, and his standing rule is that the book wins when Wanderer's Guide contradicts it. Their side is not defensible here - their own title and description say Labor Lore too.

entries.needsGuy: His standing rule covers it, but he asked to confirm every case where we deliberately differ from Wanderer's Guide.

entries.title: Poppet: fire weakness minimum 1

entries.printed: "Flammable You have weakness to fire damage equal to one-third your level (minimum 1)."
entries.wg: Their formula is level divided by three with no minimum, so a level 1 or 2 poppet takes no extra fire damage. Checked in their own data.

entries.app: Grants Goloma and Mwangi; both exist as real languages in the app.

entries.needsGuy: He asked to confirm each deliberate difference from Wanderer's Guide.

entries.question: Confirm we keep the rare Ancestry Guide android with Androffan and Common, rather than Wanderer's Guide's common Starfinder version. Yes or no?
entries.printed: "Languages Androffan Common Additional languages equal to your Intelligence modifier (if positive)." The same page records rarity "Rare" and source "Ancestry Guide".

entries.title: Wishes for Riches: dragon or leech

entries.title: Streetfood Vendor: Crafting, or a choice of Crafting or Society
entries.question: Does this background grant Crafting outright, or let the player choose between Crafting and Society?
entries.printed: "You're trained in the Crafting skill, and the Cooking Lore skill. You gain the Seasoned skill feat." The page's structured fields say the same: Crafting, Cooking Lore. No choice is printed anywhere on the page.
entries.wg: A picker offering Crafting or Society. The Foundry data reads it the same way.
entries.app: A choice of Crafting or Society — the app sides with Wanderer's Guide against the printed page, and the app's own description text has been rewritten to say "either Crafting or Society".
entries.recommendation: Follow the printed page: trained in Crafting and Cooking Lore, with no choice, and put the app's description text back to the printed sentence. If his own copy of the Tian Xia Character Guide prints a choice, he says so and we change it — the same as Northridge Scholar.
entries.why: Correction to the earlier note, which said the Nethys sentence is machine-built and cannot express a choice. It can, and it does: dozens of background pages in the same mirror read "You're trained in your choice of either the Athletics or the Nature skill" — Animal Wrangler, Blow-In, Teacher, Spell Seeker, Tapestry Refugee, Hermit and more. So the same generator that wrote this page would have written the choice if the book had one, which makes "trained in the Crafting skill, and the Cooking Lore skill" a plain grant. This is the same answer as Sky Rider at desk 88, where the printed "and" is not a choice either. Foundry and Wanderer's Guide both reading it as a choice is real counter-evidence, which is why his book is the tie-breaker rather than my say-so.
entries.ifYes: Change the background to grant Crafting outright, restore the printed description sentence, and write the difference from Wanderer's Guide down. If his book prints a choice, keep the app as it is and record that instead.
entries.needsGuy: Yes — two other readings of the same book disagree with the page, so his physical copy decides.

entries.title: Haunted: no skill feat granted
entries.question: Confirm we do not copy Wanderer's Guide: Haunted grants no skill feat. Yes or no?
entries.printed: You are trained in Occultism and an additional skill in which the haunting entity is well-versed, determined by the GM. No feat is named anywhere in the entry.

entries.ifYes: Nothing changes, the app already does this.
entries.needsGuy: Nothing new for him: on 2026-08-22 he ruled the book wins where Wanderer's Guide contradicts it. Here only so the difference is on the record.

entries.title: Tree Friend: Arboreal is a choice
entries.question: Confirm Arboreal stays an option the player may pick rather than being handed out automatically. Yes or no?
entries.printed: You gain the No Cause for Alarm skill feat, and you can choose Arboreal as one of your known languages.
entries.wg: Grants Arboreal outright, with no choice.

entries.title: Reborn Soul: restricted skill increases
entries.question: At 3rd, 7th and 15th level: extra increases locked to the two past-life Lores (A, Wanderer's Guide), or the normal increases forced onto them (B, print)?
entries.printed: At 3rd level, 7th level, and 15th level, you receive skill increases, which you can apply only to these Lore skills.
entries.wg: Raises both Lores to expert, master and legendary on top of the normal increases — six raises in all.
entries.app: The two typed past-life Lores and the +1 star are built. The increases are not. Our own note on the record calls them EXTRA increases and tells the player to apply them by hand, so our note quietly takes Wanderer's Guide's side.
entries.recommendation: Follow print, reading B: the normal skill increase at 3rd, 7th and 15th must go to one of the two past-life Lores. Our note has to be rewritten to match.
entries.why: The same book, Dark Archive, says "you also gain an additional skill increase, which you can apply only to…" for the thaumaturge. Reborn Soul drops the word additional, which is what makes it read as a restriction. Their reading is still defensible: it turns the background into a gift, mine turns it into a pure cost, and he has before chosen the reading that does not make a player worse.
entries.ifYes: At 3rd, 7th and 15th the player's skill increase is locked to the two past-life Lores instead of free, and the note on the record must be rewritten.
entries.needsGuy: One sentence carries both readings, and the answer is worth three skill increases either way — gained or lost.

entries.title: Teacher Ot: one pick asked twice
entries.question: Should the app ask the Survival-or-Performance question once instead of twice? And does the background stay common?

entries.why: The book grants exactly one skill, so two independent answers can only ever produce a wrong sheet. Unsponsored and Sponsored by a Village, from the same book and the same shape, already carry only one control, so there is nothing to invent.

entries.title: Wanderlust: flicker or troll choice
entries.question: Wanderer's Guide has the older printing of this background, where there is no choice at all. Keep our flicker-or-troll question from the newer printing? Yes or no.
entries.printed: "Your deviant abilities are of either the flicker or the troll classification. If you choose flicker, you gain the Overclock Senses deviant feat. If you choose troll, you gain the Titan Swing deviant feat."
entries.wg: Their copy of the background text reads "Your deviant abilities are of the troll classification. You gain the Titan Swing deviant feat." Their data matches their text: Titan Swing plus Express Rider, no branch.

entries.question: Wanderer's Guide marks this background Uncommon. The printed page carries no rarity trait, which means common. Keep common? Yes or no.
entries.printed: The record's own rarity field reads "common", and the printed traits block is empty — "<traits>" then "</traits>" with no Uncommon or Rare line, unlike the Rare backgrounds which print one.

entries.title: Northridge Scholar: Seasonal Boon frequency
entries.question: Wanderer's Guide puts "Once per Season" on the Seasonal Boon. Our copy of the printed page shows no frequency. Can you check the Season of Ghosts guide for a once-per-season rule?
entries.printed: "**Seasonal Boon** <actions string="Free Action" /> **Trigger** The party's reputation with Northridge increases; **Effect** Increase the party's reputation with Northridge by an additional 2 points" — no Frequency line. None of the six Willowshore boons prints one.
entries.wg: "Once per Season" on five of the six boons — and they also carry a general "Seasonal Boon (Standard)" that our copy of the book does not have at all.
entries.app: The app does carry the boon: a free action with the trigger and effect, no frequency. (The old note saying we had no record is out of date.)
entries.recommendation: Leave it as it is for now. If his book prints a once-per-season limit, add those words to the boon's popup only — no use counter, since the app cannot track seasons.
entries.why: Their reading is probably right. They carry a standard seasonal boon our copy of the book has no page for, so the frequency likely comes from a page Archives of Nethys never copied.
entries.ifYes: Nothing changes today; if he confirms the limit, the boon gains one line of text and no counter.
entries.needsGuy: He has the Season of Ghosts Player's Guide; our copy of the printed pages cannot settle this.

entries.title: Deviant backgrounds: one branch, not both
entries.question: On this record Wanderer's Guide already matches us. Do you still want the family rule — always ask the classification and grant only that branch? Yes or no.
entries.printed: "Your deviant abilities are of either the dragon or the troll classification. If you choose dragon, you gain the Blasting Beams deviant feat with the fire type. If you choose troll, you gain the Titan Swing deviant feat."
entries.wg: They ask "Select a Classification" with two options — Dragon grants Blasting Beams (fire), Troll grants Titan Swing. The earlier note that they grant both was wrong: it read the two grants without the question that wraps them.
entries.app: Asks dragon or troll, grants that branch's feat, and pins fire on the dragon side. Same as theirs.
entries.recommendation: Nothing to decide on this record — we already agree. The real family question is Sense of Belonging, Lost Loved One, Wanderlust and Total Power, where their copy is the older printing with no choice.
entries.why: Their text for this one is the newer printing and their data follows it. On the other four their text still reads "of the troll classification" with a single feat, which is the first printing, not a mistake.
entries.ifYes: Nothing changes here; the answer carries over to the four records where their book is older.
entries.needsGuy: One answer sets the rule for every gatewalker deviant background, which is his call.

entries.title: Bestial Clarity: enchantment, not mental
entries.question: Wanderer's Guide fires Bestial Clarity on any failed save against a mental effect. Print says enchantment, which is narrower. Keep enchantment? Yes or no.
entries.printed: "**Frequency** once per day; **Trigger** You fail a saving throw against an enchantment effect; **Effect** … You can reroll the triggering saving throw with a +2 circumstance bonus, but you must use the new result. This is a fortune effect."
entries.wg: Their trigger reads "a mental effect" — wider than print, so the reaction fires more often.
entries.app: The trigger text reads "an enchantment effect", word for word with print; once per day.
entries.recommendation: Keep enchantment, exactly as printed. Do not widen it to mental.
entries.why: Their wording reads "an mental effect", so someone typed over "an enchantment" on purpose — perhaps updating old wording. That is defensible, but the Firebrands page still prints enchantment and has not been reprinted.
entries.ifYes: Nothing changes; the reaction still reads enchantment and stays once per day.
entries.needsGuy: Only he can approve differing from Wanderer's Guide, and only he can say whether their wider word is a rewrite he wants to follow.

entries.title: Total Power: dragon or troll choice
entries.question: Wanderer's Guide has the older printing here too, with no choice. Keep our dragon-or-troll question, with Blasting Beams as electricity? Yes or no.
entries.printed: "If you choose dragon, you gain the Blasting Beams deviant feat with the electricity type. If you choose troll, you gain the Bone Spikes deviant feat."
entries.wg: Their text reads "Your deviant abilities are of the troll classification. You gain the Bone Spikes deviant feat." Their data matches their text, so no dragon branch exists.
entries.app: Asks dragon or troll; the dragon pick grants Blasting Beams and locks its damage to electricity.
entries.recommendation: Keep ours, together with the family answer at question 98: ask the classification, grant only that branch.
entries.why: They are faithful to the first Gatewalkers guide, which really had one classification. The Remastered guide added the choice, and that is the page Archives of Nethys prints.
entries.ifYes: Nothing changes; dragon players keep getting Blasting Beams with electricity damage.
entries.needsGuy: Only he can approve following the newer book, and this sits inside the deviant-background family he rules on once.

entries.title: Flexible Spellcaster: pool or per rank
entries.question: Should the spell collection be one flat pool you spread across ranks as you like (print), or fixed per rank like Wanderer's Guide (what we built)? A or B.
entries.printed: "The number of spells in your spell collection each day equals the total number of spell slots you get each day from your class spells." The printed table gives one Collection number per level — 4 at level 3 — and the only limit stated is "you must select at least one 1st-level spell for your collection each time you prepare".
entries.wg: Forces a per-rank list: as many collected spells at each rank as slots at that rank. Their own copy of the text still quotes the flat rule.
entries.app: We now build the collection, but per rank — the same shape as Wanderer's Guide.
entries.recommendation: Follow print: one flat pool sized by total slots, with at least one 1st-rank spell required. This needs new engine work.
entries.why: Their shape is always a legal collection, just never the only one. The "at least one 1st-level spell" line would be pointless if every rank were already fixed, and it takes real choices away from the player.
entries.ifYes: A level-3 cleric could collect one 1st-rank and three 2nd-rank spells, instead of being forced into two and two.
entries.needsGuy: Only he can decide whether the flat pool is worth building a new kind of spell list the app has never had.

entries.title: Divine font: rank 9 at 19-20
entries.question: At levels 19 and 20, should the cleric's divine font slots stay 9th rank (ours) or rise to 10th rank (Wanderer's Guide)? A or B.
entries.printed: Miraculous Spell: "You gain a single 10th-rank spell slot… Unlike with other spell slots, you can't use 10-rank slots with abilities that give you more spell slots or that let you cast spells without expending spell slots."
entries.wg: Raises the font to 10th rank at levels 19-20; every other level matches ours.
entries.app: Font stays at 9th rank; the code deliberately leaves rank 10 out of the font's reach.
entries.recommendation: Keep ours, rank 9. Miraculous Spell bars the 10th-rank slot from abilities that grant extra slots, and the font is one.
entries.why: Reading the font's own line alone, at 19th your highest rank of cleric slot really is 10th — that is their reading and it is fair. The Miraculous Spell sentence exists to stop exactly that, and it wins.
entries.ifYes: Nothing changes; a 19th-level cleric keeps six 9th-rank heal or harm slots.
entries.needsGuy: Only he can sign off on the app disagreeing with Wanderer's Guide on a level-19 cleric's slot count.

entries.title: Magus: which book, and therefore which slot table
entries.question: Does the magus keep only the two highest ranks of spell slots, or every rank?
entries.printed: The 2021 Secrets of Magic table empties the lower ranks as you level — at 5th level a magus has 2 slots of 2nd rank and 2 of 3rd, and none of 1st. The 2026 Impossible Magic table in the same mirror holds 2 slots at every rank once unlocked, keeping the lower ones. Both tables are in our copy.
entries.wg: They keep 2 slots at every rank from 5th level on, which is the 2026 table.
entries.app: Only the two highest ranks hold slots, which is the 2021 table.
entries.recommendation: Answer this with desks 56, 120 and 121 as one book decision. If the magus moves to the 2026 Impossible Magic printing — which our copy holds in full — the magus keeps its lower-rank slots and Wanderer's Guide is right. Keeping the app as it is means staying on the 2021 book, which would contradict desk 121's move of this same class onto the 2026 text.
entries.why: Correction to the earlier note, which said the remastered class page carries the same table and that Nethys strips it. It does not: the 2026 page prints all twenty rows and they disagree with the 2021 rows from 5th level onward. Read side by side, at 5th level the 2021 magus has no 1st-rank slots and the 2026 magus has two. So this is not Wanderer's Guide contradicting the book — it is the two of us on different books. The app cannot be on the 2021 table for slots and the 2026 text for Studious Spell.
entries.ifYes: Move the magus to the 2026 printing whole — slot table, archetype spellcasting feats and the new Studious Spell feature — together with the summoner. Existing magus characters gain their lower-rank slots back.
entries.needsGuy: Yes — it changes existing magus characters, and it must be the same call as the summoner.

entries.title: Animist: 7th-rank slots at 13-18
entries.question: Wanderer's Guide gives one 7th-rank slot at levels 13 to 18. The printed table gives more, and we match it. Keep ours? Yes or no.
entries.printed: The Animist Spells per Day table reads, in the 7th-rank column, "1+1" at level 13, "2+1" at 14 to 16, and "2+2" at 17 to 18. Its note: "The number before a plus sign indicates your spell slots via animist spellcasting, and the number after it indicates your spell slots from apparition spellcasting."
entries.wg: One 7th-rank slot in total across both pools at levels 13-18.
entries.app: Two at level 13, three at 14 to 16, four at 17 to 18 — the printed table exactly, at every level and every rank.
entries.recommendation: Keep ours. The printed table is in our copy after all, and it matches us row for row.
entries.why: The earlier note said the table was missing; it is not. Their single slot matches no row of it, so there is no defensible reading on their side here.
entries.ifYes: Nothing changes; the animist keeps the slot counts the book prints.
entries.needsGuy: Only because it differs from Wanderer's Guide — the book itself is settled, so he does not need to look anything up.

entries.title: Bone Magic: cantrip list width
entries.question: Bone Magic's cantrip picker: offer both the occult and primal lists (print, ours), or narrow it to the tradition the player answered (Wanderer's Guide)? A or B.
entries.printed: "Choose one cantrip from either the occult spell list or the primal spell list… **Special** Choose when you gain this feat whether your innate spells are primal or occult; this choice applies to all innate spells you gain from lizardfolk ancestry feats that have Bone Magic as a prerequisite."
entries.wg: Asks the tradition first, then shows only that tradition's cantrips in the picker.
entries.app: One picker holding all 56 common occult and primal cantrips; the answer only sets the casting tradition.
entries.recommendation: Keep the printed union of both lists.
entries.why: Their narrowing is a fair reading of "your innate spells are primal or occult" — but that clause says how the spell is cast, and the first sentence plainly offers either list.
entries.ifYes: Nothing changes; a lizardfolk who answers primal can still pick an occult-only cantrip and cast it as primal.
entries.needsGuy: Barely his at all — his standing note already says the menu's contents are ours to decide. It reaches him only because it differs from Wanderer's Guide.

entries.title: Acute Vision: darkvision while raging
entries.question: Should barbarian Acute Vision give darkvision only while Rage is on (print, ours), or always (Wanderer's Guide)? A or B.
entries.printed: "When you are raging, your visual senses improve, granting you darkvision."
entries.wg: Grants a permanent Darkvision ability; it sits on the sheet whether or not the barbarian is raging.
entries.app: Darkvision appears in Senses only while the Rage toggle is on, and the Rage card lists it.
entries.recommendation: Keep ours: darkvision only while raging, shown on the Rage card.
entries.why: Their always-on version is simpler and never wrong mid-rage, but it hands the sense to a barbarian standing still. His own rule says a benefit that depends on something is not a flat value — and here the app can see Rage.
entries.ifYes: Nothing changes; darkvision keeps appearing and disappearing with the Rage toggle.
entries.needsGuy: Only he can approve differing from Wanderer's Guide on a sense the player sees on the sheet.

entries.title: Guardian's Armor: toggle or automatic
entries.question: Should the resistance show on its own whenever medium or heavy armour is worn, instead of the player flipping a toggle? A: automatic. B: keep the toggle.
entries.printed: While wearing medium or heavy armor, you gain resistance to physical damage equal to 1 + half your level.
entries.wg: Gives the physical resistance always, with no armour condition at all.
entries.app: A mode the player switches on by hand; nothing shows on the sheet until they do.
entries.recommendation: Show the resistance automatically while medium or heavy armour is worn, and drop the toggle. Never Wanderer's Guide's always-on version.
entries.why: Five inventor armour features already work this way in the app: the resistance is there while the armour is on. Guardian's Armor is the odd one out.
entries.ifYes: A guardian in plate sees the resistance without touching anything, and loses it when the armour comes off.
entries.needsGuy: Three other records say 'while wearing medium or heavy armor' and would change with it, and some players may already use the toggle.

entries.title: Spellmaster: whose focus tradition
entries.question: Should the two Spellmaster focus spells use the character's own tradition and attribute, or a fixed Arcane/Intelligence one like Wanderer's Guide? A: the character's own. B: fixed Arcane.
entries.printed: The feat names no tradition. Its prerequisite is "ability to cast focus spells", and the general rule says "you need to use the attribute modifier determined by the source of the focus spell".
entries.aonDoc: feat/feat-1134 and feat/feat-2241; the general rule is rules/rules-2231
entries.wg: Builds a separate Arcane, Intelligence focus source and hangs both spells on it.
entries.app: Both spells join the character's own focus spells, using their tradition and attribute.
entries.recommendation: Keep ours. The prerequisite guarantees the character already casts focus spells, so these two use the ones they have.
entries.why: The printed rule does say the granting ability sets the tradition, which is their excuse. But Spellmaster sets none, so theirs is invented while ours uses what the character already has.
entries.ifYes: Nothing changes; a cleric Spellmaster still casts both spells as divine off Wisdom.
entries.needsGuy: The book leaves a hole here, so only he can say whether an archetype borrows the character's tradition or gets one of its own.

entries.title: Empathic Calm: one spell or both
entries.question: Print says "either calm emotions or sanctuary". Keep the player's single pick, or grant both like Wanderer's Guide? A: one pick. B: both.
entries.printed: Once per day, you can cast either calm emotions or sanctuary as an innate occult spell, heightened to half your level rounded up.
entries.wg: Grants both spells, once each per day, and asks the player nothing.
entries.app: Asks the player to pick one; the pick becomes the once-per-day occult innate spell.
entries.recommendation: Keep ours, one pick. This matches his ruling #1 on Backup Runic Enhancement, where he chose the printed single choice over Wanderer's Guide's both.
entries.why: "Either... or" is one spell, and he has already ruled this exact shape once.
entries.ifYes: Nothing changes; the player still picks Calm or Sanctuary.
entries.needsGuy: Only he can confirm his earlier single-choice ruling is meant to cover every "X or Y" feat, not just that one record.

entries.title: Colugo's Traversal: one spell or both
entries.question: Print says "your choice of gentle landing or jump". Keep the single pick, or grant both like Wanderer's Guide? A: one pick. B: both.
entries.printed: You can cast your choice of gentle landing or jump as a primal innate spell once per day. At 9th level, these spells are heightened to 3rd rank.
entries.wg: Grants both gentle landing and jump, one cast each, with no choice offered.
entries.app: One pick; the chosen spell is a once-per-day primal innate, 3rd rank from level 9.
entries.recommendation: Keep ours, one pick. Same answer as Empathic Calm; one word from him should settle every "your choice of X or Y" feat.
entries.why: "Your choice of" names one spell. Their only foothold is the plural "these spells" in the next sentence, which is just covering both options.
entries.ifYes: Nothing changes; the player still picks Gentle Landing or Jump.
entries.needsGuy: Only he can confirm one answer covers the whole family of these feats rather than each being asked separately.

entries.title: Oatia Skysage: which cantrips offered
entries.question: Restrict the two cantrip picks to Detect Magic, Guidance, Know the Way and Read Aura as printed, or keep offering all 38 occult cantrips?
entries.printed: You gain a spell repertoire with two of the following cantrips of your choice: detect magic, guidance, know the way, or read aura.
entries.wg: Filters on a trait no cantrip in their own data has, so it lists nothing or everything.
entries.app: Offers all 38 occult cantrips, with no restriction.
entries.recommendation: Restrict the picker to the four printed cantrips.
entries.why: Print names exactly four, and Wanderer's Guide's filter matches no cantrip in their own data, so there is nothing to copy.
entries.ifYes: New Oatia characters are offered four cantrips instead of 38. An existing character who picked something else would have to choose again.
entries.needsGuy: Barely his: his standing rule already gives us the filtering of choice menus, and his Q9 says the builder offers only what the player may pick. He need only object.

entries.title: Undine: swim Speed 10
entries.question: Keep the unconditional 10-foot swim Speed as printed, or copy Wanderer's Guide's condition, which gives nothing to a non-swimmer? A: keep ours. B: copy theirs.
entries.printed: You gain a swim Speed of 10 feet and the amphibious trait.
entries.wg: A condition that gives no swim Speed to a non-swimmer and caps a faster one at 10.
entries.app: Swim Speed 10, always, plus the amphibious trait. Matches print.
entries.recommendation: Keep ours. Print is unconditional, and the book has won before where Wanderer's Guide's data contradicts it.
entries.why: Their condition leaves the very character the heritage exists for with no swim Speed. The kindest reading of theirs is a cap at 10, which print never asks for.
entries.ifYes: Nothing changes; the app already does this.
entries.needsGuy: His standing rule is to match Wanderer's Guide exactly, so only he can confirm this is one of the cases where the book wins.

entries.title: Mightyfall Kobold: two boosts or three
entries.question: Print replaces the kobold's boosts with Strength, Charisma and an Intelligence flaw: two boosts. Wanderer's Guide leaves the free boost in, making three. Keep ours?
entries.printed: Instead of the normal attribute boosts and flaws, you can choose to gain a boost to Strength, a boost to Charisma, and a flaw in Intelligence.
entries.wg: Adjusts four attributes on top of the normal kobold set, leaving the free boost: three boosts.
entries.app: Replaces the whole set: a Strength boost, a Charisma boost, an Intelligence flaw. The extra ancestry Hit Points are there too.
entries.recommendation: Keep ours. "Instead of the normal attribute boosts" replaces all of them, so the ancestry's free boost goes too.
entries.why: "Instead of" is a replacement. Theirs only works if "the normal boosts" is read as the fixed ones and not the free one, which the sentence does not say.
entries.ifYes: Nothing changes; a Mightyfall kobold keeps two boosts, not three.
entries.needsGuy: Their version is a whole boost stronger, so only he can decide the app keeps the weaker printed build.

entries.title: Born of Animal: Speed 30 condition
entries.question: Print gives Speed 30 only in Yaoguai Form with both hands free. Keep it as a starred note, or add Wanderer's Guide's always-on +5 Speed?
entries.printed: Yaoguai Form You can dash like an animal. If you have both hands free, you can increase your Speed to 30 feet as you run on all fours.
entries.wg: A flat, always-on +5 Speed on top of the 25-foot yaoguai Speed.
entries.app: A star on the Speed row explaining the 30-foot dash and its conditions.
entries.recommendation: Keep ours. The dash is a choice made at the table, so his rule makes it a star, not a number.
entries.why: The sheet can see empty hands, but it cannot see whether you are running on all fours, and that is half the condition.
entries.ifYes: Nothing changes; the Speed row keeps its star.
entries.needsGuy: Hunter Automaton prints the very same sentence and is starred the same way, so one word settles both.

entries.title: Grave Orc: minimum 1 resistance
entries.question: Keep the printed minimum of 1 void resistance at levels 1 to 3, or drop it to match Wanderer's Guide's plain half-level? A: keep ours.
entries.printed: You gain resistance to void damage equal to half your level (minimum 1).
entries.wg: Half your level with no minimum, so zero void resistance at levels 1 to 3.
entries.app: Half your level, never below 1. Matches print.
entries.recommendation: Keep ours. Print says minimum 1, and their own Stormtossed Tengu row shows they do encode that minimum elsewhere.
entries.why: It is a missed line on their side, not a different reading of the rule.
entries.ifYes: Nothing changes; a level 1 grave orc keeps resistance 1.
entries.needsGuy: Matching Wanderer's Guide exactly is the standing rule, so only he can wave this through as their mistake.

entries.title: Deny Lady Nanbyo: bulk thresholds
entries.question: Print moves the encumbered limit by 1 and the maximum by 2. Wanderer's Guide moves both by 2. Keep ours? A: keep ours. B: copy theirs.
entries.printed: Your vow grants you the strength to carry 1 more Bulk than normal before becoming encumbered and up to a maximum of 2 more Bulk
entries.wg: A single value of 2, which moves the encumbered threshold by 2 as well.
entries.app: Encumbered +1, maximum +2. Already built, despite the question saying nothing was authored.
entries.recommendation: Keep ours. Print gives two different numbers and the app already carries both correctly.
entries.why: They reused their Hefty Hauler value, and Hefty Hauler's printed text really does move both thresholds by the same amount.
entries.ifYes: Nothing changes; the app already ships +1 encumbered and +2 maximum.
entries.needsGuy: Only he can accept a one-point difference from Wanderer's Guide on a carried-weight number.

entries.title: Waning Moon Sarangay: reroll skill
entries.question: Print applies the once-a-day reroll to whichever skill you chose. Wanderer's Guide names Acrobatics on every option. Keep ours? A: chosen skill. B: their wording.
entries.printed: Once per day, when you roll a critical failure with the chosen skill, you can reroll the check, taking the new result, even if it's worse.
entries.wg: Their Crafting and Performance options both say the reroll fires on an Acrobatics check.
entries.app: The reroll follows the chosen skill, and the note already sits on that skill's row.
entries.recommendation: Keep ours. Nothing to build; the note on the chosen skill is already there.
entries.why: Their Acrobatics wording is a copy-paste slip, and their own option descriptions say Crafting and Performance.
entries.ifYes: Nothing changes.
entries.needsGuy: Only he can wave through a difference from Wanderer's Guide, even one this plainly a slip on their side.

entries.title: Summoner: which book, and therefore which slot table
entries.question: Does the summoner lose its lower-rank spell slots as it levels, or keep them?
entries.printed: The 2021 Secrets of Magic summoner has "two spell slots each of your two highest spell ranks" and loses the lower ones. The 2026 Impossible Magic summoner table holds 2 slots at every rank once unlocked — at 5th level, 2 of 1st, 2 of 2nd and 1 of 3rd. Both are in our copy.
entries.wg: They keep every lower rank at 2 slots, which is the 2026 table, and 77 of their slot rows differ from the app's.
entries.app: Only the two highest ranks hold slots, which is the 2021 rule.
entries.recommendation: Move the summoner to the 2026 Impossible Magic reprint, together with the magus (desks 56, 104 and 121). Its slot table keeps the lower ranks, so on that book Wanderer's Guide agrees with the printed page and the app does not.
entries.why: Correction to the earlier note, which said the reprint's slot table is not in our copy and that the exact numbers would have to come from Wanderer's Guide. The table is there: the 2026 page prints all twenty rows, and from 5th level it holds 2 slots at every rank once unlocked. So no number has to be taken from another app — which matters, because he has already refused once to build a number out of another source alone. The app already ships this same book's necromancer and runesmith; the magus and summoner are the last two classes still on the 2021 book, and the 2026 pages for both are complete in our copy.
entries.ifYes: Move the summoner to the 2026 printing whole — slot table and archetype spellcasting feats — together with the magus. Existing summoner characters gain their lower-rank slots back.
entries.needsGuy: Yes — it changes existing summoner characters, and it must be the same call as the magus.

entries.title: Studious Spells: the free Arcane Cascade
entries.question: Should casting a studious spell let you use Arcane Cascade as a free action?
entries.printed: The 2021 Studious Spells feature prints no such clause. The 2026 Impossible Magic feature, renamed Studious Spell, prints it outright: "When you cast a studious spell, you can use Arcane Cascade as a free action as your next action this turn." It also arrives at 7th level rather than 1st, and lists spells instead of granting extra slots.
entries.wg: They add the free Arcane Cascade to every studious spell at all three tiers.
entries.app: Nothing. Arcane Cascade costs one action and no free-action version exists for any spell.
entries.recommendation: Adopt the rider — as one decision with desks 56, 104 and 120, not on its own. Wanderer's Guide is quoting the current printed wording, from the same book whose necromancer and runesmith the app already ships.
entries.why: Read in the mirror and confirmed word for word. But the whole feature changed in that reprint, not just this sentence: it is renamed Studious Spell, it arrives at 7th level, and it lists spells rather than granting extra slots. Taking this one sentence while leaving the magus on the 2021 slot table would put the app on two books at once, which is why it has to ride with the magus and summoner decision rather than being answered by itself.
entries.ifYes: Move the magus to the 2026 printing whole — slot table, archetype spellcasting feats and the rebuilt Studious Spell feature with its free Arcane Cascade — together with the summoner.
entries.needsGuy: Yes — it is one quarter of a single decision about which book these two classes are on.

entries.title: Speed bonuses: type and plural
entries.question: Should Speed bonuses carry a type, so two status bonuses take the highest instead of adding up? And should a feat be able to raise all Speeds, not just walking?
entries.printed: You gain a +5-foot status bonus to your Speeds; this increases to a +10-foot status bonus while you have panache.
entries.wg: Records the status type on Swashbuckler's Speed, but has only one Speed value, so it cannot do all Speeds.
entries.app: Adds every Speed bonus together, untyped, and only to walking Speed. Twenty records carry one today.
entries.recommendation: Follow print on both: give Speed bonuses a type so two status bonuses take the highest, and let a clause raise all Speeds.
entries.why: Print names the bonus type and says Speeds, and two status bonuses never add up, so the app shows too much Speed today. Wanderer's Guide records the type too, so only the all-Speeds half goes beyond them.
entries.ifYes: A monk or barbarian who also takes Swashbuckler's Speed loses the 5 feet the app was wrongly adding.
entries.needsGuy: It re-does all twenty existing Speed records and lowers numbers on characters already built, and the all-Speeds half goes further than Wanderer's Guide can go.

entries.title: Haunting Memories: second daily pick
entries.question: Should the app also hand out Haunting Memories' temporary skill feat each morning? And cap that feat at half your level (print) or 10 (Wanderer's Guide)?
entries.printed: You also gain one skill feat with a minimum requirement of your new rank in the chosen skill. For the purpose of meeting level prerequisites for this feat, your level is equal to half your level.
entries.wg: Offers a real second pick: any skill feat of level 10 or lower.
entries.app: Only the proficiency pick. The feat half is a note that grants nothing.
entries.recommendation: Yes, ask both questions, and use print's half-your-level cap. Nothing new is needed: let the feat hand over a small feature carrying the second morning question, the way the wizard's daily feat pick already works.
entries.why: Print asks two things at daily preparations. The app can already ask a second one this way, and you have ruled that what a menu offers is ours to choose, so the cap follows print rather than their flat 10.
entries.ifYes: A ghost-archetype player picks a temporary skill feat each morning instead of reading a note and applying it by hand.
entries.needsGuy: It adds a second question to your daily preparations screen, and the list will be any skill feat up to the cap — the app cannot tell which feats demand that skill at that rank.

entries.title: Dream Magic taken twice
entries.question: Should a repeatable feat remember each taking separately, so Dream Magic's second taking gives the other spell? If no, cap it at one taking with a note.
entries.printed: Special You can take this feat twice, gaining the spell you didn't select initially the second time.
entries.wg: One pick per taking; each option grants one of the two spells.
entries.app: Both takings share one answer, so a player who takes it twice still gets one spell.
entries.recommendation: Follow print. The app can already do it: move the pick onto the feat's own question, which is remembered per taking and can be told to force the other answer the second time.
entries.why: Print says the second taking gives the spell you did not choose, and today that second taking adds nothing. Thirty-eight feats already use that per-taking question, and a repeatable feat already hands over a once-a-day spell through it.
entries.ifYes: A sleepwalker who takes the feat twice gets both Dream Message and Sleep instead of only one.
entries.needsGuy: Less than it looked: print settles it and the app has the parts. Say yes and it is a data fix, with no saved character disturbed and no re-asking.

entries.title: Glyph Expert: which traps
entries.question: Keep print's narrower trigger, where the save upgrade only fires against traps with magical writing, or widen it to any magical trap the way Wanderer's Guide does?
entries.printed: traps that feature magical writing... When you attempt a saving throw against the effects of these traps, if you roll a success, you get a critical success instead
entries.wg: Fires the save upgrade against any magical trap, with no magical-writing wording at all.
entries.app: Already matches print: the upgrade fires only against traps that feature magical writing.
entries.recommendation: Keep print, and record it as a deliberate difference from Wanderer's Guide under your standing rule that the book wins.
entries.why: You already ruled that where their data contradicts the printed text, the book wins. Their wider trigger may simply be that sentence hung on the magical-trap save bonus they already had, rather than a different reading of the feat.
entries.ifYes: Nothing changes, the app already does this.
entries.needsGuy: Your standing rule is to match Wanderer's Guide exactly, so only you can confirm the book-wins exception covers this one.

entries.title: Divine Breadth: extra cantrip?
entries.question: Wanderer's Guide gives an extra cantrip slot that print never mentions. Follow them, or keep print and grant no cantrip?
entries.printed: Increase the spell slots you gain from cleric archetype feats by 1 for each spell rank other than your two highest cleric spell slots.
entries.wg: Adds one cantrip slot at every level, on top of Cleric Dedication's two.
entries.app: No cantrip. One extra slot per rank except the two highest, exactly as printed.
entries.recommendation: Keep print, no cantrip. Rule once for the whole Breadth family and apply it to Primal and Occult Breadth too.
entries.why: Print has no cantrip clause. Their extra entry is one copy shared by three Breadth feats and missing from Arcane, which reads like a slip — though their reading is arguable if you count cantrips as a spell rank.
entries.ifYes: Nothing changes, the app already does this.
entries.needsGuy: Only you can say whether one shared entry copied across three feats is their mistake or their deliberate reading.

entries.title: Primal Breadth: extra cantrip?
entries.question: The druid half of the same question. Follow Wanderer's Guide's extra cantrip slot, or keep print and grant no cantrip?
entries.printed: Increase the spell slots you gain from druid archetype feats by 1 for each spell rank other than your two highest druid spell slots.
entries.wg: The identical extra cantrip entry, the same copy as Divine Breadth's, aimed at druid.
entries.app: No cantrip. One extra slot per rank except the two highest, exactly as printed — the same shape on all four Breadth feats.
entries.recommendation: Keep print, no cantrip, same answer as Divine Breadth. One ruling covers Divine, Primal and Occult, the three feats carrying that copied entry.
entries.why: It is literally the same entry as Divine Breadth's — I counted it three times in their data — and print has no cantrip clause.
entries.ifYes: Nothing changes, the app already does this.
entries.needsGuy: Same call as Divine Breadth; you may prefer to answer the whole family once rather than feat by feat.

entries.title: Necromantic Tenacity: which effects
entries.question: Which trigger ships: print's "a necromancy effect", Wanderer's Guide's "death or void trait", or both together? Pick A, B, or both.
entries.printed: If you roll a success on a saving throw against a necromancy effect, you get a critical success instead; if you roll a critical failure on such a save, you get a failure instead.
entries.wg: The same two upgrades, but triggered by the death or void traits.
entries.app: The same two upgrades, triggered by a necromancy effect, print's wording word for word.
entries.recommendation: Keep print's necromancy wording; the feat has never been reprinted. If you want it to still do something at a newer table, the middle road is to fire on either wording.
entries.why: Your standing rule is that the book wins. But their reading is defensible: the word necromancy no longer exists in the current rules, so a strict print reading may almost never fire.
entries.ifYes: Nothing changes today; the middle road would also fire on death and void effects.
entries.needsGuy: Only you can say whether the app should quietly modernise a feat Paizo never reprinted.

entries.title: Spore Order counts as Leaf Order
entries.question: Should a spore-order druid qualify for leaf-order feats, and should the app start refusing druids who do not?
entries.printed: "The spore order is a variant of the leaf order. If you have the spore order, you count as a member of the leaf order, and you qualify for leaf order feats. Your familiar must be a fungus leshy." Cultivation Order prints the same sentence.
entries.wg: Their Spore Order hands over their whole Leaf Order feature and then marks the druid's order as spore, with the skill and the order spell hung off that mark.
entries.app: The skill, the focus spell and the granted feat all agree with print. The membership itself was added in an earlier batch and already works.
entries.recommendation: Already done — nothing to build, and one answer covers this desk, its duplicate at desk 139, and Cultivation Order at desk 144. Spore and Cultivation already count as members of the Leaf Order for the ten feats that ask for it, and nothing is blocked. Keep the blocking switched off and close all three.
entries.why: Correction to the earlier note, which described this as still to be decided. Checked in the app: the membership shipped in an earlier batch and adds leaf-order to what the character counts as having, for both spore and cultivation, with the printed sentence quoted beside it. It only adds, so no druid is newly refused. Switching blocking on would start refusing ten feats no druid has ever been refused, and would wrongly refuse a druid who took their order another way. Do not copy Wanderer's Guide's route of handing over the whole Leaf Order feature — that also gives Leaf's own skill and focus spell, which this order does not print.
entries.ifYes: Close this desk entry, its duplicate at desk 139 and Cultivation Order at desk 144 with one word. Nothing to build.
entries.needsGuy: No — it is built, it matches the printed sentence, and it refuses nobody. It only needs closing.

entries.title: Gleaming Blade transcendence name
entries.question: Keep the printed name Flowing Spirit Strike only, or also carry Wanderer's Guide's name Mirrored Spirit Strike as an alternative label so their imports match?
entries.printed: Transcendence Two Actions (Spirit, Transcendence) Flowing Spirit Strike; Effect Make two Strikes with the gleaming blade, each against the same target and using your current multiple attack penalty.
entries.wg: Calls it Mirrored Spirit Strike, a name that appears nowhere in the whole Nethys archive.
entries.app: Uses the printed name Flowing Spirit Strike, with the printed effect.
entries.recommendation: Keep the printed name only. Do not carry their name; it exists nowhere in the rules and would only confuse a player.
entries.why: You already ruled to use whichever wording leaves the player least confused, and their name is not a real rules name.
entries.ifYes: Nothing changes, the app already does this.
entries.needsGuy: Only you can weigh whether smooth Wanderer's Guide imports are worth showing a name Paizo never printed.

entries.title: Barrow's Edge: damage wording
entries.question: Wanderer's Guide makes the extra damage persistent and drops the bigger damage against a wounded foe. Confirm we keep print instead?
entries.printed: The barrow's edge deals 1 additional spirit damage per weapon damage die... If the creature is below half its maximum Hit Points, the weapon deals 3 additional spirit damage per weapon damage dice instead.
entries.wg: 1 persistent spirit damage per die, and no extra damage against a foe below half Hit Points.
entries.app: +1 spirit damage per die, or +3 per die against a foe below half its Hit Points.
entries.recommendation: Keep print. Their version is wrong twice in one sentence, and the book wins under your standing rule.
entries.why: Persistent damage and additional damage are different rules, and their version also drops a whole printed clause.
entries.ifYes: Nothing changes, the app already does this.
entries.needsGuy: Your standing rule is to match them exactly, so only you can confirm the book-wins exception applies here.

entries.title: Gaze Sharp as Steel: transcendence
entries.question: Wanderer's Guide replaces the printed transcendence with a Reactive Strike grant. Confirm the app keeps print's extra precision damage and offers no alternative anywhere?
entries.printed: Transcendence Single Action (Concentrate, Prediction, Transcendence) A Moment Unending... Your next successful Strike against an enemy before the end of your next turn deals an additional 1d6 precision damage.
entries.wg: Grants the Reactive Strike feat until your next turn instead of any damage.
entries.app: A Moment Unending as printed: 1d6 precision damage, rising to 2d6 at 10th and 3d6 at 18th.
entries.recommendation: Keep print and offer no alternative. Their version is a different ability wearing the printed name.
entries.why: This is not them doing less than the book; it is a completely different effect, which your book-wins rule covers.
entries.ifYes: Nothing changes, the app already does this.
entries.needsGuy: Only you can confirm that replacing an effect outright is the book-wins case rather than something to copy.

entries.title: Dragon eidolon: tradition picker
entries.question: Print fixes a dragon eidolon's tradition as arcane. Wanderer's Guide offers all four. Keep arcane fixed, or add their picker?
entries.printed: Tradition Arcane
entries.wg: A four-way picker: arcane, divine, occult or primal.
entries.app: Arcane, fixed, with no picker anywhere.
entries.recommendation: Keep arcane fixed. If you ever want their four-way pick it has to be built as a small picker on the eidolon — nothing in the app today, the Overrides card included, can change an eidolon's tradition.
entries.why: Print names one tradition with no alternative, and you already ruled the book wins and that what a menu offers is ours. Their picker has no printed basis; it only helps a table that wants the freedom.
entries.ifYes: Nothing changes for a normal build; a Wanderer's Guide dragon summoner with another tradition arrives as arcane, with no control to change it.
entries.needsGuy: Only you can decide whether losing a tradition on import matters enough to build a picker the book does not print.

entries.title: Spore Order: the same question, filed twice
entries.question: Should a spore-order druid qualify for leaf-order feats, and should the app start refusing druids who do not?
entries.printed: "The spore order is a variant of the leaf order. If you have the spore order, you count as a member of the leaf order, and you qualify for leaf order feats. Your familiar must be a fungus leshy."
entries.wg: Their Spore Order hands over their whole Leaf Order feature and then marks the druid's order as spore.
entries.app: The skill, the focus spell and the granted feat all agree with print, and the membership itself was added in an earlier batch and already works.
entries.recommendation: Same as desk 134 and desk 144, and it is already done — nothing to build. Spore and Cultivation already count as members of the Leaf Order, nothing is blocked, and the blocking stays off. This entry is a duplicate; answer all three with one word.
entries.why: Correction to the earlier note, which left this open at medium confidence. Checked in the app: the membership shipped in an earlier batch, for both spore and cultivation, and it only adds to what the character counts as having, so no druid is newly refused anything. Desk 144 already reports the same thing about Cultivation Order, so the three entries were pointing three different ways at one finished piece of work.
entries.ifYes: Close desks 134, 139 and 144 together. Nothing to build.
entries.needsGuy: No — it is built and matches print. It only needs closing.

entries.title: Scar of the Survivor: the dying value never moves
entries.question: The app cannot move a death threshold from a toggle. Add one (A), or leave Diehard as text the player applies by hand (B)?
entries.printed: Immanence: "Divine energy spreads outward from your scar, reinforcing your flesh. You gain the benefits of the Diehard feat and a +1 status bonus to Fortitude saving throws."
entries.wg: Nothing mechanical at all - only the printed paragraph as text. No evidence either way.
entries.app: Checked: the old always-on Diehard grant is gone. A note on your Fortitude line mentions Diehard; the dying value itself never moves.
entries.recommendation: A - give the ikon a divine-spark toggle that really raises the dying value, like the three immanence toggles already shipped. The same shape also fixes Soul Well, whose one-minute effect today raises your dying value permanently.
entries.why: His own rule says a switchable effect belongs in a toggle, and a toggle is where the other immanence ikons keep their numbers. Today the Diehard note sits on Fortitude, which is not the number it changes. B costs nothing but leaves the player doing it by hand.
entries.ifYes: While your divine spark is in the scar, you die at dying 5 instead of 4, and the sheet shows it.
entries.needsGuy: Print settles the rule but not where the app should keep it, and the change touches shared engine files plus a screen no one owns.

entries.title: Skybearer's Belt: bonus versus Bulk aura
entries.question: Follow the printed +1 bonuses (A), or follow Wanderer's Guide's 15-foot ally Bulk aura (B)?
entries.printed: "You can attempt to Disarm, Grapple, Shove, or Trip creatures up to two sizes larger than you, and you gain a +1 circumstance bonus to checks for these actions and to your saving throws to resist these actions."
entries.wg: Prints a different rule: a 15-foot aura letting allies carry 4 more Bulk. Drops the +1 entirely.
entries.app: Three +1 stars - Athletics, Fortitude, Reflex - each while your divine spark is in the belt. Checked in the code; all three come from the one printed sentence.
entries.recommendation: A - keep the printed bonuses and record their Bulk aura as a known difference so it stops coming back. His 2026-08-22 rule: where they contradict print, the book wins.
entries.why: No ikon in the book mentions carrying extra Bulk anywhere, and their version is loose text with nothing behind it. Their wording might come from some unreleased version, but nothing printed supports it.
entries.ifYes: Nothing changes for a player; the record simply stops being re-checked in every future comparison.
entries.needsGuy: Only he can allow a permanent, standing difference from Wanderer's Guide, even one that follows the book.

entries.title: Echo of Lost Moments: the 5th spell
entries.question: Print and the app both put Illusory Scene at 5th; Wanderer's Guide grants a different spell. May I record theirs as a mistake so it stops coming back?
entries.printed: "Apparition Spells - Cantrip Figment - 1st Déjà Vu - 2nd Dispel Magic - 3rd Curse of Lost Time - 4th Vision of Death - 5th Illusory Scene"
entries.wg: Grants Illusory Disguise, a rank-1 spell, on the 5th rung of the ladder.
entries.app: Grants Illusory Scene at 5th. Checked: the whole ten-spell ladder matches print exactly, rung for rung.
entries.recommendation: Mark it as a known difference - print and the app agree, and the spell they hand over is a rank-1 spell sitting on the 5th rung. Same call as his rule that the book wins.
entries.why: The printed ladder is unambiguous and nothing on our side needs changing.
entries.ifYes: Nothing changes for a player; the record stops being re-checked in every future comparison.
entries.needsGuy: An agent may not close a Wanderer's Guide conflict on its own, even an obvious one; that call is his.

entries.title: Time oracle curse: the penalty is conditional
entries.question: The penalty has nowhere to live. Add four Time-only cursebound toggles (A), let a mystery's curse add its own penalty to the shared toggle (B), or leave it as text (C)?
entries.printed: "You take a status penalty to your AC against attacks made against you from reactions or free actions and a status penalty to saving throws against effects that would make you fatigued or slowed equal to your cursebound value."
entries.wg: Sixteen numeric rows, one set per cursebound stage: -1/-2/-3/-4 to AC and to all three saves, with the printed conditions written beside them as text.
entries.app: A note on AC and a note on saves, each saying the penalty and when it applies. The numbers on the sheet do not move.
entries.recommendation: C - leave it as the note it is today. Both halves only apply in one narrow spot each, and his 2026-08-22 rule is that anything conditional is a note, not a number.
entries.why: Print drops your AC only against attacks from reactions or free actions, and your saves only against being fatigued or slowed. A real number would penalise the oracle against everything. If he wants the exact number per stage shown, the app already has a way to show a number inside a toggle without moving the total.
entries.ifYes: Nothing changes for a player, and the oracle keeps a correct AC and correct saves against everything print does not name.
