entries.title: Cultivation and Spore count as leaf
entries.question: Should the app enforce leaf-order membership for Cultivation and Spore druids (A), simply know it without blocking anything (B), or keep saying nothing (C)?
entries.printed: "The cultivation order is a variant of the leaf order. If you have the cultivation order, you count as a member of the leaf order, and you qualify for leaf order feats."
entries.wg: Hands the druid an empty "Leaf Order" record, so the name appears but nothing mechanical happens.
entries.app: Already built. Checked: the app counts a Cultivation or Spore druid as a leaf druid, and the ten leaf-order feats are still refused to nobody, for any druid.
entries.recommendation: B - and it is already done, so there is nothing to build. Keep blocking switched off.
entries.why: The membership was added in an earlier batch. Switching blocking on would start refusing ten feats no druid has ever been refused, and would wrongly refuse an Order Explorer druid.
entries.ifYes: Nothing changes; the app already knows a Cultivation or Spore druid is also a leaf druid.
entries.needsGuy: Only he can decide whether the app should begin refusing feat picks it has always allowed, for every druid of every order.

entries.title: Spider instinct: the Web attack
entries.question: Should the spider's Web become a real attack row that does no damage (A), an item as Wanderer's Guide does (B), or stay as text on Rage (C)?
entries.printed: "The spider's web attack deals no damage, but the target takes a -10-foot circumstance penalty to its Speeds for 1 round on a hit."
entries.wg: Hands the raging barbarian two items - spider fangs and spider web - rather than attack rows.
entries.app: Fangs only. Checked: 31 granted attacks on this feature, no Web. The Web rides as text on the Rage action.
entries.recommendation: A - allow an attack with no damage, so Web becomes a real row you can roll. It also houses every other damageless attack in the books.
entries.why: Every attack row in the app demands a damage die and a damage type, so a damageless attack needs both made optional. Their item version is cheaper, but an inventory line for a body part reads oddly and still cannot be rolled.
entries.ifYes: A spider-instinct barbarian gets a rollable Web attack with its speed penalty, instead of a note to apply by hand.
entries.needsGuy: Print settles that Web exists but not how the app should model it, and this changes the attacks screen every character sees.

entries.title: Six pages lost printed sections
entries.question: Six pages lost printed sections in the last data rebuild. Run the repair now (A), or build a second protected file so a rebuild cannot undo it (B)?
entries.printed: "Sorcerous Gifts - Cantrip Detect Magic - 1st Force Barrage - 2nd Dispel Magic - 3rd Haste - 4th Translocate - 5th Scouting Eye - 6th Disintegrate - 7th Retrocognition"
entries.wg: Not a difference. They carry the missing deed names as real records, agreeing with print.
entries.app: Checked today: all six pages are still missing their spell lists and deed names.
entries.recommendation: A - just run the repair. The durable half already exists: the data rebuild now ends with the repair script, and a check in the verify run catches it if it is ever skipped.
entries.why: B would build a second protected file for a problem that was already fixed after this question was written. What is actually left is one run of a repair the rebuild now does by itself.
entries.ifYes: Players get the missing spell lists and deed names back on six pages, and every future rebuild keeps them.
entries.needsGuy: The content is not in doubt, and agents are not allowed to run repair scripts - only he, or whoever runs the build, can do it.

entries.title: Values worked out, not chosen
entries.question: When print works a value out from the character and Wanderer's Guide asks the player instead, do we keep working it out and show no control (A), or add the pick (B)?
entries.printed: "You gain resistance equal to 3 + half your level to negative damage, or to positive damage if you have negative healing (such as if you're a dhampir)."
entries.wg: Asks two questions: pick a resistance (void or vitality), and pick a sanctification (holy, unholy, or none).
entries.app: Works it out from the character. Checked: a level-20 inventor gets spirit 13 and void 13 automatically, with no control shown.
entries.recommendation: A - make this a permanent standing exception. Where print works the value out from the character and Wanderer's Guide asks, we keep working it out and show no control, as battle-creed already does.
entries.why: The printed text offers the player nothing to choose, and his 2026-08-22 rule is that where they contradict print, the book wins. Their pick would only help if the app could not see a character's void healing or sanctification, and it can see both.
entries.ifYes: Nothing changes for a player; the app stops raising records like this, and the earlier battle-creed decision stands.
entries.needsGuy: It sets a permanent exception to his own standing rule that every Wanderer's Guide question must appear as a visible control on our side.

entries.title: Hyper Boosters: +30 needs legendary
entries.question: Print gives the +30 only if you are legendary in Crafting; Wanderer's Guide gives it to everyone in Overdrive. Confirm print stands (A)?
entries.printed: "which increases to a +20-foot status bonus when you're in Overdrive. If you're legendary in Crafting, it instead increases to a +30-foot status bonus when you're in Overdrive."
entries.wg: Their +30 fires at any Crafting rank the moment Overdrive is on - a mistake in how they wrote the condition.
entries.app: +10 Speed, +20 in Overdrive. Checked: Hyper Boosters and Speed Boosters each add 5 standing and 5 more in Overdrive, which is exactly the printed total. The legendary +30 shows as a note.
entries.recommendation: A - print stands and the app is right. Record their version as a mistake in their data so this record stops coming back in every comparison.
entries.why: The Crafting half of their test is true for every character, so their +30 really depends on Overdrive alone. A non-legendary inventor would get 30 feet where print gives 20.
entries.ifYes: Nothing changes for a player; the record stops being re-checked in every future comparison.
entries.needsGuy: Only he can allow a standing difference from Wanderer's Guide, even one that simply follows the printed book.

entries.title: Playtest rows are not evidence
entries.question: Should a Wanderer's Guide record marked (playtest) never count as evidence about the released version (A), or should we read it as evidence anyway (B)?
entries.printed: Print is silent: Spirit Walk prints no sense clause at all. Its prerequisite, Apparition Sense, prints "You have apparition sight, an imprecise sense that allows you to detect the presence of invisible or hidden spirits, haunts, and undead within 30 feet of you."
entries.aonDoc: feat/feat-7120 (Spirit Walk itself is feat/feat-7137, which prints no sense clause)
entries.wg: Two rows share the name; only the playtest one has a mechanic, granting a precise 30-foot sense.
entries.app: Checked: no sense on Spirit Walk. Apparition sight sits on Apparition Sense, imprecise, 30 feet, exactly where print puts it.
entries.recommendation: A - a row marked (playtest) is never evidence about the released record. Their released Spirit Walk row carries nothing, so it tells us nothing about the released feat.
entries.why: Reading playtest text as if it were print has already produced three false alarms, and the released book is the authority.
entries.ifYes: Nothing changes for a player; the app stops chasing playtest wording that was never published.
entries.needsGuy: Only he can set a standing reading rule for a whole class of Wanderer's Guide records rather than one at a time.

entries.title: Chronomancer's Secrets: Stasis is focus
entries.question: Print calls Stasis a domain spell, which is a focus spell; Wanderer's Guide gives it as an ordinary spell. Confirm print stands (A)?
entries.printed: "The secrets of time peel back, revealing deeper truths. You gain either the stasis domain spell or the path of least resistance focus spell."
entries.wg: Gives Stasis as an ordinary spell, from their old record, under a menu titled "Select a focus spell".
entries.app: Both options grant a focus spell. Checked: Stasis carries the focus trait, and the feat's own focus point is not counted twice.
entries.recommendation: A - print stands and the app is right. Record their version as a mistake in their data so it stops coming back; their own menu title already says focus spell.
entries.why: A domain spell is a focus spell, the printed sentence calls the other option a focus spell in the same breath, and the app's Stasis record carries the focus trait.
entries.ifYes: Nothing changes for a player; the record stops being re-checked in every future comparison.
entries.needsGuy: Only he can allow a standing difference from Wanderer's Guide, even one that simply follows the printed book.

The printed quote was the wrong sentence - it quoted only the base case, while the deciding clauses are the two 'if you're already trained' sentences that follow. Replaced with the full text. Recommendation stands. Quote verbatim from feat-8528, and AoN marks feat-3245 as superseded, so the repoint is right. Confirmed the app has a counter of 4 vials and no pyrotechnic item, and does ship a Versatile Vial item to copy. Changed: the app already displays the current printed text (only the book link is stale), and I checked the knock-on of repointing - the Alchemical Crafting feat the app grants comes from the shared 'quick alchemy benefits' rule, which the new printing still uses, so nothing is lost.

Recommendation stands - quote verbatim from feat-8812, no armor clause anywhere in it. But the 'why' was wrong. The older Character Guide and World Guide dedications do not grant light, medium or heavy armor training either; they grant Hellknight plate armor specialization and an armor-conditional Intimidation bonus. Wanderer's Guide's armor training is printed - in Armiger's Protection (feat-8814), a separate Hellknight feat with exactly their conditional shape, which the app already builds. Rewrote 'why' and 'ifYes' to say that, and kept the note that their always-expert Intimidation is the Character Guide wording.

Recommendation stands and I checked the direction of the two printings carefully, since the source labels in the mirror are misleading. feat-3053 is dated 2025-02-18 (Guns & Gears Remastered) and has no +2; feat-8555 is dated 2021-10-13 and has the +2 and an expert Crafting requirement. Changed: clearer wording, added that the remaster also lowered the requirement to trained, and noted the app's shown description is already the new text.

The recommendation was wrong. 'Keep the app, no change' does not hold. Reading the two carriers and the code that consumes them: the Crafting grant carries the redundant-grant fallback flag, which fires whenever Crafting is already trained, while the Specialty Crafting grant fires on the same condition and is skipped only when the character already holds that feat. So a character already trained in Crafting but without Specialty Crafting gets the feat AND a free skill - the book says the feat replaces the Crafting training, with the free skill reserved for someone who has both. Two of three cases are right; the middle one over-delivers. Rewrote the recommendation, app description and 'why', and dropped confidence to medium because this comes from reading the code, not from running a build.

The print check holds: both equipment-2734 and equipment-34 have completely empty bodies, and the quoted line matches the record's text field exactly. Changed the recommendation. Reworded to: keep it inert, and if it must not look blank, say plainly that the book prints no rules for it rather than writing flavour of our own.

groups.label: Which printing wins — follow the newest printing our copy of Archives of Nethys actually holds, and follow it whole
groups.recommendation: One rule for all of them. The app follows the newest printing that is actually in our copy of Archives of Nethys, and it follows that printing whole — never a mix of two books on one record. Where Wanderer's Guide is on an older book, keep the app and do not add the old book's extras (Devil Allies, Fear No Law, Hellknight Dedication, Ardent Armiger, Reverse Engineer's +2, Wishes for Riches, and all five Gatewalkers deviant backgrounds). Where the older book has a sentence the newer one deliberately dropped, do not add it back (Steady Balance's Grab an Edge clause). Where our copy holds only the older page, that page is what the app follows even if a newer book exists somewhere else (Android, Bestial Clarity, Necromantic Tenacity). And point each record at the page of the printing it actually follows — Firework Technician to feat-8528, not the superseded feat-3245. Advanced Red Mantis Magic is the one that breaks this rule today and is corrected below.

groups.label: Magus and Summoner — one book decision behind four separate questions
groups.recommendation: Answer these four together as a single decision, because they are the same question asked four times. Our copy of Archives of Nethys holds the complete 2026 Impossible Magic Magus and Summoner: the two class pages with their full twenty-row slot tables, the archetype spellcasting feats, and the new Studious Spell feature. The app already ships that same book's Necromancer and Runesmith — the magus and summoner are the last two classes on the 2021 book. Move both to the 2026 printing whole: they keep their lower-rank spell slots instead of losing them as they level, their archetypes use ordinary spellcasting instead of the old bounded rule (and the basic feat drops from level 6 to level 4), and Studious Spell gains the printed free Arcane Cascade. On that book Wanderer's Guide is right on all four points and the app is on superseded text. This is Guy's call because it changes existing magus and summoner characters — but it has to be one call, not four.

groups.label: Wanderer's Guide contradicts the printed page — the book wins, and the difference gets written down
groups.recommendation: These are all the same decision under his 2026-08-22 rule: where Wanderer's Guide's data contradicts the printed text, the book wins and the app stays as it is. Nothing to build in any of them. The one thing to add for consistency: every one of them gets written down as a known, deliberate difference from Wanderer's Guide, so the comparison stops raising the same record again. Today only about six of these say that, which is why several of them are on his desk for a second time. Two worth naming: Instinct Ability's flat +3 Hit Points is one slice of how they pay out Barbarian Resiliency, which his R11 ruling already covers, so copying it would pay twice; and Haunted grants no skill feat in either printing, so their grant has no printed source at all rather than an old one.

groups.label: The printed page is silent — never invent a number
groups.recommendation: Where the printed page says nothing, the app writes nothing. A number that appears only in Wanderer's Guide, only in Foundry, or only in a playtest document is not evidence about the printed record — he has already refused a Foundry-only number once. So: Merchant's Scale stays inert, the Zealot Staff loses its once-per-minute limit, the Skybearer's Belt keeps its printed bonuses and their Bulk aura is recorded as a difference, and a row marked playtest is never evidence. Three still need his word because the silence itself is the question: Benefactor's Resistance (the app floors the resistance at 1 where the page says a plain 'half your level', so at 1st level a strict reading gives 0), Mask of the Mantis Major (the Major block does not restate the spell rank, so it either carries the Greater's 5th rank forward or falls back to the base 2nd), and Northridge Scholar (his physical book may print a once-per-season limit our copy does not carry).

groups.label: One printed choice, asked once, at the moment the book asks it
groups.recommendation: One printed choice means one control in the app. Where the book says 'during your daily preparations', the control lives in Daily preparations and defaults to yesterday's answer — his Q23 answer. Where the book asks once while building the character, it lives in the builder. Delete every second control asking the same question: Nagaji Spell Familiarity's dead build-time picker, the Dusty Rose Prism's duplicate, and Teacher Ot's second skill control. All six kitsune and nagaji spell feats get the same shape — one question at daily preparations granting a 1st-rank innate spell once a day, on the tradition and spell list the feat prints. Where the book genuinely asks a second thing (Haunting Memories) or a different answer on a second taking (Dream Magic), that is a real second question and gets its own control.

groups.label: The value is worked out from the character — never a picker
groups.recommendation: Make the Otherworldly Protection answer the permanent standing rule and apply it to all six. Where the printed sentence works something out from the character — the tradition you already cast in, your own spell slots, your own sanctification or void healing — the app works it out and shows no control at all. Where the printed sentence names one answer outright, the app keeps that one answer (the dragon eidolon's arcane tradition). Wanderer's Guide's pickers in these six have no printed basis; three of the four options on their Time Mage picker are traditions the character cannot legally have. Filtering what a menu offers is his to decide, but inventing a menu the book does not print is not.

groups.label: A conditional value is a star or a mode, never a flat number
groups.recommendation: One test for all five, from his 2026-08-22 rule. If the sheet can see the condition, the app applies the value only while it holds and shows it where the player will look — Acute Vision's darkvision on the Rage card, Guardian's Armor's resistance shown automatically while medium or heavy armour is worn (never Wanderer's Guide's always-on version, and no toggle, since five inventor armour features already work this way). If the sheet cannot see the condition, the value is a star or a note carrying the printed sentence and no number moves — Favored Terrain's Speed, Born of Animal's Speed 30, and the time oracle's curse, whose two halves each apply in one narrow spot.

groups.label: A control whose answer reaches nothing is a missing piece — build the piece, do not approximate it
groups.recommendation: His Q26 answer covers all of these: a question whose answer does nothing is usually a missing piece to build, not decoration. Build the small piece rather than substituting an easier grant that gives the player more than the book does — never training in medium and heavy armour to make an AC come out right, never Additional Lore to stand in for a plain Lore, never a flat number in place of a computed one. Where the piece would let someone pick something they cannot take, show the option greyed out saying why rather than hiding it, which is his Q27 answer. Hardened Chassis is the one to watch: the automaton rules say you get no enhancement unless a feat grants it, so it must never be a question every automaton is asked.

groups.label: Armour that 'uses your highest armour proficiency'
groups.recommendation: One answer for both kineticist impulses. The stone armour and the hardwood armour use the wearer's best armour proficiency by themselves, on the medium and the heavy version alike, and the kineticist gains no training in medium or heavy armour. The borrowing idea already exists in the app — Sentinel Dedication and Mountain Skin both use it — but today it is attached to a whole armour category; these two need the same idea attached to the armour the impulse hands over. Do not copy Wanderer's Guide's shortcut of training the kineticist in medium and heavy armour: it makes the AC come out right and also lets them wear real plate and half plate, which the book never gives them.

groups.label: 'Your choice of X or Y' means exactly one
groups.recommendation: One spell, one pick — the same call he already made on Backup Runic Enhancement. One word from him here covers every feat printing 'either… or' or 'your choice of X or Y', so these should never come back one record at a time.

groups.label: The 'already trained in it' branch is read literally, branch by branch
groups.recommendation: Read each printed branch on its own and build exactly what it says. A free skill is the fallback only where the book prints one. Molten Wit: pair the skill and the feat only in the base case; someone trained in one must take the other skill and may pick either feat; someone trained in both gets a free skill of their choice and may pick either feat. Intuitive Crafting: someone already trained in Crafting who does not yet have Specialty Crafting gets the feat only, because the book's replacement there is the feat, not a skill — the app currently hands out a free skill whenever Crafting is already trained.

groups.label: The seven Unifying Emblems must behave the same way
groups.recommendation: One answer covers all seven, and today's state is the one answer that is certainly wrong. Checked in the app's own data: four of the seven already carry their once-per-day spell (Lyrune, Shadde, Shriikirri and Skoan) and three carry none (Shundar, Sklar and Tamiir), so the same item behaves differently depending on the clan. Either finish the family by adding Thoughtful Gift, Concordant Choir and Tailwind, or take the spell off the four that have it. The printed Activate line points at finishing it; his R10 rule (match Wanderer's Guide even where they do less, and they do nothing here) points at removing it. Sklar-Quah also has no activation cost at all today and should take its spell's own 1-to-3 actions.

groups.label: The note goes on the record the player actually reads
groups.recommendation: One rule. Never rewrite a printed spell name. Put the feat's or item's extra sentence on the entry the player opens when it matters — the three aeon stones' resonant sentence on augury, shield and illusory disguise as well as on the wayfinder mark, and Toppling Tentacles' note on Black Tentacles as printed. Correction worth knowing: none of the three stones grants a second spell, so the old worry about a double grant was a misreading; the Dusty Rose Prism's second picker is simply a duplicate and should go. Where the remaster replaced the spell the feat names, add one short line clearly marked as ours naming the replacement, and attach the feat's mechanical rider to that replacement only where the effect still makes sense against it — it does for Slither, it does not for Light, where the feat would cut an all-day spell down to one minute.

groups.label: Keep the printed scope — neither widened nor narrowed
groups.recommendation: The printed sentence's own words fix the scope, and neither side may move them. Melee means melee (Brutality). Order of the Gate means only that order (Locate Lawbreakers), which matters because another feat lets Hellknights of any order take that same benefit. Advanced firearms sit in the expert sentence, not the master one (Gunslinger Mastery). 'Instead of the normal attribute boosts' replaces all of them, the free one included (Mightyfall Kobold). Shoony Lore is Shoony Lore, not Additional Lore with its three extra skill increases. Bone Magic offers both cantrip lists, because the tradition clause says how the spell is cast, not which list it comes from. Oatia Skysage offers exactly the four printed cantrips. Weapon Expertise is printed separately per class and needs no ruling at all. What a menu offers is his standing call to make, but the printed scope is not ours to widen.

groups.label: Backgrounds — the printed page decides whether it is a grant or a choice
groups.recommendation: Read the printed page and take it at its word. Archives of Nethys writes 'you're trained in your choice of either the X or the Y skill' on dozens of background pages, so its background text can and does express a choice — which means a page reading 'trained in the Crafting skill, and the Cooking Lore skill' is a flat grant. So Sky Rider grants both skills as printed, and Streetfood Vendor should be Crafting, flat. The app currently says 'either Crafting or Society' and has rewritten its own description text to match, siding with Wanderer's Guide against the page. Because Foundry reads it as a choice too, his own copy of the Tian Xia Character Guide is the tie-breaker — the same way Northridge Scholar waits on his book.

groups.label: Adventure-path backgrounds stay common
groups.recommendation: One answer for all five. Rarity comes from a printed trait on the page, and none of these five prints one, so all five stay common. Wanderer's Guide's Uncommon is a consistent house choice about campaign-only content rather than a data slip, but the book does not print it. Teacher Ot has a separate problem in the same record: the book grants one skill and the app asks for it twice, so drop the second control and keep the one the granted feat already follows.

groups.label: The Breadth feats grant no cantrip
groups.recommendation: One ruling covers Divine, Primal and Occult Breadth — the three sharing the same copied entry in Wanderer's Guide — and Arcane Breadth, which does not have it. No printed Breadth feat has a cantrip clause, so none of them grants a cantrip. Their extra entry reads as an authoring slip rather than a different reading.

groups.label: Spore and Cultivation Order count as Leaf Order — already built
groups.recommendation: One answer, and it is already done. Checked in the app: both Spore and Cultivation already count as members of the Leaf Order for the ten feats that ask for it, added in an earlier batch, and it only adds — no druid is newly refused anything. Keep the blocking switched off, close all three desk entries, and do not copy Wanderer's Guide's route of handing over the whole Leaf Order feature, which would also give Leaf's own skill and focus spell that these orders do not print.

groups.label: Innate spells reach expert at 12th by the general rule
groups.recommendation: Both follow the printed Innate Spells rule — trained, rising to expert at 12th level — and the app already does exactly that in both cases. Nothing to build; close both. Sequestered Spell keeps its single narrowed picker, since what a menu offers is already his to decide.

groups.label: Wording — whichever leaves the player least confused
groups.recommendation: His Q12 answer covers both. Screech Shooter: give each grade its own sentence carrying only that grade's numbers, so one popup never shows DC 25 and DC 30 together. Gleaming Blade: print only the real rules name — a name that exists nowhere in the rules can only confuse.

groups.label: The animist slot table — the same record on the desk twice
groups.recommendation: These are one question asked twice. The printed table is in our copy after all and it matches the app row for row: the first 7th-rank slot at 13th level, 8th at 15th, 9th at 17th. Wanderer's Guide is a level late and their single slot matches no row of the table. Keep the app and close both.

flags.why: The recommendation suggests showing a line saying the book prints no rules for this item. That line is ours, not printed. If it goes anywhere it must be visibly marked as ours and must never be written into the record's printed description — the same rule that Wild Lights breaks today.

Adding the once-per-day spell to the three empty emblems goes past Wanderer's Guide, who encode nothing for the spell on any of the seven; the other whole answer, removing the spell from the four that have it, goes against the printed Activate line. Either way one of his own rules gives. Covers desks 29 and 30 as well.

Raising the Major mask to 5th rank is an inference, not a printed number: the Major block restates the item bonus and adds pinpoint but never restates the spell rank. Verified in the mirror — only the Greater block prints "heightened to 5th-rank". Either the rank carries forward from the Greater or it falls back to the base 2nd. The app currently shows 2nd, which matches neither reading. Low confidence, and his word settles it.

Reading Reborn Soul's skill increases as restricted turns the background into a pure cost. It rests on the absence of one word ("additional") that the thaumaturge version prints and this one does not, so print does not decide it. The entry itself notes he has before chosen the reading that does not make a player worse. His word, not a reading.

The "middle road" of firing on either the old necromancy wording or the current one is wider than the printed feat, which has never been reprinted. Following it would make the app do more than the page says. The strict print reading is the safe one; anything wider is his to allow.

judgeNotes: Read the authorities first: work/owner-questions.json (ruled[] R1-R11 and the three authorised exceptions) and docs/gold-set-answers.md. The three rules doing most of the work here are the 2026-08-22 rule that the book wins where Wanderer's Guide contradicts it, the 2026-08-22 rule that a conditional value is a star and not a number, and R10 (matching Wanderer's Guide where they simply do less). Five findings were checked against the mirror and the app's own data rather than taken from the entries: (1) the 2026 Impossible Magic Magus and Summoner pages, their slot tables, their archetype spellcasting feats and the new Studious Spell feature are ALL in our copy of Archives of Nethys, which turns desks 56, 104, 120 and 121 into one book decision and removes the need to take any number from Wanderer's Guide; (2) Spore and Cultivation counting as Leaf Order is already built and refuses nobody, so desks 134, 139 and 144 are one closed question, not three open ones; (3) the app's best-armour-proficiency borrowing does exist and is used by Sentinel Dedication and Mountain Skin, but is attached to an armour category rather than to a granted armour item, which reconciles the two contradictory claims at desks 10 and 26; (4) Nethys background pages do express skill choices in so many words on dozens of records, so Streetfood Vendor's flat sentence is a grant and desk 82's defence of the app fails; (5) four of the seven Unifying Emblems carry their daily spell and three do not, exactly as desks 28 to 30 describe. The single largest consistency gain available is the magus and summoner book decision: four separate desk entries currently point three different ways at one question.
